units.text:
Lesson 2.3 · Concept
Some syndromes show on the skin first.
A handful of inherited endocrine syndromes appear on the skin before the glands declare themselves. In multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1), multiple facial angiofibromas and collagenomas are common. In Carney complex, lentigines on the lips, eyelids and canthi, blue naevi and small skin myxomas sit alongside myxomas of the heart and cortisol-secreting adrenal disease. In MEN2A, an itchy, rippled, pigmented plaque between the shoulder blades can precede medullary thyroid cancer.
MEN1: facial angiofibromas, collagenomas
Carney complex: lip and eyelid lentigines, myxomas
MEN2A: lichen amyloidosis between the shoulder blades
Narration: Some endocrine syndromes are written on the skin years before the glands give them away. In multiple endocrine neoplasia type one, most patients in one careful series had several facial angiofi…
units.sourceNote: Darling 1997 · Kirschner 2000 · Correa 2015 · Stanescu 2024 · Lause 2017 · the guide's inherited-syndromes chapter

assertions.text: In multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1), facial angiofibromas and collagenomas are common, with most patients in one series exhibiting multiple facial angiofibromas and collagenomas.
assertions.quote: Multiple facial angiofibromas were observed in 28 (88%) of the patients with MEN1, with 16 patients (50%) having 5 or more. Angiofibromas were clinically and histologically identical to those in individuals with tuberous sclerosis. Collagenomas were observed in 23 patients (72%).
assertions.note: Darling et al. found facial angiofibromas in 88% and collagenomas in 72% of MEN1 patients.

assertions.text: The facial angiofibromas seen in MEN1 are clinically and histologically identical to those seen in tuberous sclerosis.
assertions.quote: Angiofibromas were clinically and histologically identical to those in individuals with tuberous sclerosis.
assertions.note: Angiofibromas in MEN1 are described as clinically and histologically identical to those in tuberous sclerosis.

assertions.text: Carney complex is usually caused by inactivating variants in the PRKAR1A gene.
assertions.quote: More than 70% of the patients diagnosed with CNC carry mutations on the PRKAR1A gene (CNC1 locus) and this percentage increases to 80% for those with Cushing’s syndrome due to primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease (PPNAD).
assertions.note: Over 70% of Carney complex patients harbor inactivating PRKAR1A variants.

assertions.text: In Carney complex, lentigines on the lips, eyelids, and canthi, blue naevi, and cutaneous myxomas occur alongside cardiac myxomas and cortisol-secreting adrenal disease.
assertions.quote: The result is a distinctive skin picture (perioral and eyelid lentigines, multiple blue nevi, and cutaneous myxomas) paired with endocrine overactivity: ACTH-independent Cushing from primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease (PPNAD), acromegaly, and thyroid tumors.[4]
assertions.note: The guide notes that inactivating PRKAR1A variants produce perioral and eyelid lentigines, blue nevi, and cutaneous myxomas paired with PPNAD-driven Cushing syndrome.

assertions.text: In MEN2A, cutaneous lichen amyloidosis presents as an itchy, rippled, pigmented patch between the shoulder blades and can precede medullary thyroid cancer.
assertions.quote: Its skin clue is cutaneous lichen amyloidosis: pruritic, rippled, hyperpigmented plaques over the upper back and interscapular region that cluster with RET codon-634 variants — in effect a visible marker of medullary-thyroid-cancer risk.[3]
assertions.note: The guide notes that pruritic, rippled, hyperpigmented plaques over the interscapular region can precede medullary thyroid cancer.

units.text:
The evidence
Eighty-eight per cent.
In a consecutive series of 32 people with MEN1 examined at the US National Institutes of Health, 88% had multiple facial angiofibromas and 72% had collagenomas. The angiofibromas were clinically and histologically identical to those of tuberous sclerosis. The authors concluded that angiofibromas in someone without tuberous sclerosis call for biochemical testing for MEN1.
of 32 people with MEN1 had multiple facial angiofibromas
Darling et al., 1997 — collagenomas in 72%
What it means: Multiple facial angiofibromas are common in MEN1 and can be its first visible sign; in someone without tuberous sclerosis they are a reason for endocrine testing, whatever the cosmetic plan.
What it does not mean: It does not mean a single facial papule is MEN1. This is one small referral-centre series, and angiofibromas have other causes, tuberous sclerosis above all.

units.text:
Concept
The everyday endocrine signs.
Most endocrine skin signs you meet come from common disease. New generalised darkening, strongest in skin creases, scars, mucosa and sun-exposed skin, can signal primary adrenal insufficiency, which can turn into a life-threatening crisis. Hirsutism that appears fast, keeps progressing, or comes with a deepening voice or clitoromegaly makes an androgen-secreting tumour more likely. Velvety dark plaques of acanthosis nigricans track insulin resistance, pretibial myxoedema points to Graves' disease, and cold, dry skin suggests hypothyroidism.
Darkening in creases, scars and gums: adrenal insufficiency
Rapid hirsutism or virilization: exclude a tumour
Acanthosis, pretibial plaques, dry cool skin: metabolic and thyroid
Narration: Most of the endocrine skin signs you will actually meet come from common conditions. New, generalised darkening, most obvious …

assertions.text: New generalised darkening, strongest in skin creases, scars, mucosa, and sun-exposed skin, can signal primary adrenal insufficiency.
assertions.quote: Whatever the cause, the skin sign is the same and is mechanistically elegant: loss of cortisol feedback drives POMC-derived ACTH and α-MSH, so melanocortin signaling rises and the patient develops hyperpigmentation — darkest in palmar creases, scars, and mucosa — with congenital adrenal hyperplasia adding androgen-driven hirsutism and acne.[1]
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni (2026) explains that primary adrenal insufficiency causes hyperpigmentation that is darkest in palmar creases, scars, and mucosa.

assertions.text: The Endocrine Society recommends testing for primary adrenal insufficiency in patients with indicative symptoms, suggesting a low diagnostic and therapeutic threshold in acutely ill patients.
assertions.quote: We recommend diagnostic tests for the exclusion of primary adrenal insufficiency in all patients with indicative clinical symptoms or signs. In particular, we suggest a low diagnostic (and therapeutic) threshold in acutely ill patients, as well as in patients with predisposing factors.
assertions.note: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends exclusion testing in symptomatic patients and suggests a low diagnostic and therapeutic threshold in acutely ill patients.

assertions.text: Suspected adrenal crisis must be treated before test results return because treatment delay increases mortality risk.
assertions.note: The provided abstract and sources do not mention treating before results return or the mortality risk associated with diagnostic delay.

recheck.note: The provided source texts do not state that suspected adrenal crisis must be treated before test results return or that treatment delay increases mortality risk.

assertions.quote: — Rapidly progressive virilization (deepening voice, clitoromegaly, rapid hirsutism) — possible androgen-secreting tumor.
assertions.note: The guide notes that rapidly progressive virilization, including rapid hirsutism, deepening voice, and clitoromegaly, suggests an androgen-secreting tumor and warrants prompt referral.

assertions.text: Velvety dark plaques of acanthosis nigricans track insulin resistance.
assertions.quote: Growth hormone and IGF-1 promote fibroblast proliferation, collagen synthesis, and dermal thickness; IGF-1 also stimulates sebaceous activity, part of why high-glycemic, high-insulin states track with acne,[9] while marked insulin resistance surfaces cutaneously as acanthosis nigricans.
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni (2026) states that marked insulin resistance surfaces cutaneously as acanthosis nigricans.

assertions.text: Pretibial myxoedema points to Graves' disease.
assertions.quote: Hypothyroidism gives dry, coarse, cool skin and myxedema; hyperthyroidism gives warm, moist skin and, in Graves' disease, pretibial myxedema.[8]
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni (2026) notes that hyperthyroidism in Graves' disease presents with pretibial myxedema.

assertions.text: Cold, dry, coarse skin suggests hypothyroidism.
assertions.quote: Hypothyroidism gives dry, coarse, cool skin and myxedema; hyperthyroidism gives warm, moist skin and, in Graves' disease, pretibial myxedema.[8]
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni (2026) notes that hypothyroidism causes dry, coarse, and cool skin.

units.text:
Fictional case
Freckles before the wedding.
A 29-year-old asks for laser removal of 'freckles' on her lips and at the corners of her eyes before her wedding. You notice a soft, skin-coloured papule on one eyelid. She mentions her father had 'a heart tumour' removed in his thirties. This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence; choose the first move that fits it.
Lip and canthal lentigines: typical of Carney complex
Eyelid papule: a possible cutaneous myxoma
A family heart tumour: the reason not to wait
Narration: Consider a fictional patient, built from this lesson's evidence. She is twenty-nine and wants the freckles on her lips and at the corners of her eyes lasered before her wedding. While you examine her you notice a soft, skin-coloured bump on one eyelid. She mentions that her father had a heart tumour removed in his thirties. Pigmented spots at the corners of the eyes…

assertions.text: Pigmented spots at the corners of the eyes are seen in Carney complex and Peutz–Jeghers syndrome.
assertions.quote: inner or outer canthal pigmentation such as the one shown here is only seen in CNC and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome making it diagnostic for these two conditions.
assertions.note: Correa (2015) notes that inner or outer canthal pigmentation is seen in Carney complex and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

assertions.text: Small skin myxomas favour the eyelids and ears.
assertions.quote: Cutaneous myxomas (Figure 1D–F) are found in 30–55% of CNC patients and usually appear in the eyelid, external ear canal, breast nipples, and the genitalia .
assertions.note: Correa (2015) states that cutaneous myxomas typically appear on the eyelid, external ear canal, breast nipples, and genitalia.

assertions.text: In Carney complex, tumours of the heart cause more than half of the deaths.
assertions.quote: They are responsible for more than 50% of the mortality of the disease , Myxomas can completely occlude a valvular orifice and may cause sudden death .
assertions.note: Correa (2015) confirms that cardiac myxomas account for more than 50% of mortality in Carney complex.

units.text:
What do you do first?
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Proceed with the laser: lentigines are benign and she has a deadline.
Explanation: The spots may well be benign. Their distribution, the eyelid papule and the family history are what matter, and together they flag a possible syndrome.
Correct answer: Pause the cosmetic plan, document the findings and family history, and refer her promptly for endocrine and genetic assessment.
Explanation: Right. Canthal and lip lentigines with a possible myxoma and a family cardiac tumour fit Carney complex, where early echocardiographic screening matters. You route; the specialist diagnoses.

assertions.text: Early echocardiographic screening is essential in Carney complex.

This is why early detection and regular screening with echocardiography are essential ; cardiac CT or MRI may also be used for the detection of these tumors, especially in post-operative hearts with altered anatomy .

assertions.note: Correa et al. confirm that primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease causes ACTH-independent overproduction of cortisol in Carney complex.

units.text:
Closing Module 2: which statement keeps mechanism, evidence, regulation and the open question apart?
Explanation: Keep the four registers apart for hormones exactly as you do for peptides.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Estrogen raises dermal collagen, so hormone therapy is indicated for skin ageing.
Explanation: That blends mechanism into indication. The collagen effect is real in small trials; the approved uses are symptoms and bone.
Correct answer: Estrogen acts on skin receptors (mechanism); small trials show thicker skin, while the largest found no wrinkle difference (evidence); US approved uses are symptoms and bone (regulation); whether longer treatment changes facial ageing is untested (open question).
Explanation: Correct. Four separate answers, each with its own source.

assertions.text: Estrogen acts on receptors in human skin.
assertions.quote: Surprisingly, no significant changes in production were observed in women or men after 2-week estradiol treatment of photoaged forearm or face skin, despite similar expression of estrogen receptors (ER-alpha, ER-beta, and GPR30) in aged and photoaged skin.
assertions.note: The study confirms the expression of estrogen receptors in human skin.

assertions.text: Small clinical trials show that estrogen treatment increases skin thickness.
assertions.quote: Treatment with conjugated estrogens for 12 months significantly increases, at the level of the right great trochanter, the thickness of the skin (p < 0.01), as assessed by ultrasonography, and of the dermis (p < 0.05), as assessed by skin biopsy.
assertions.note: Conjugated estrogen treatment significantly increased skin and dermal thickness in postmenopausal women.

assertions.text: The largest trial found no statistically significant difference in facial wrinkling between hormone therapy and placebo.
assertions.quote: There were slight decreases in all parameters for all treatment groups for the primary subject end points, but there were no statistically significant differences between the NA/EE groups and placebo.
assertions.note: The 485-subject RCT found no significant differences in wrinkling compared to placebo.

assertions.text: US FDA-approved indications for menopausal hormone therapy are menopausal symptoms and prevention of bone loss.
assertions.quote: The FDA has approved multiple hormone therapies for moderate-to-severe hot flashes, vaginal dryness and discomfort, and preventing bone loss.

units.text:
Mechanism
The skin keeps its own fat.
Beneath the dermis lies subcutaneous fat. Within the reticular dermis itself sits a thinner layer, dermal white adipose tissue. In mice, this layer expands rapidly after a Staphylococcus aureus infection, its new fat cells release the antimicrobial peptide cathelicidin, and the capacity fades with age through TGF-β signalling. Human skin arranges this fat differently, in cones around hair follicles, and human acne lesions contain perifollicular preadipocytes that make cathelicidin. What the layer contributes to human skin ageing has not been measured.
A second fat layer inside the dermis
In mice: antimicrobial, and lost with age
In people: a different shape, and an open question about ageing
Narration: Most people picture skin fat as one layer under the dermis. There is a second, thinner layer inside the reticular dermis itself, called dermal white a…
units.sourceNote: Zhang 2015, 2019 · Chen 2019 · Kruglikov & Scherer 2016 · O'Neill 2022 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 11

assertions.text: Within the reticular dermis itself sits a layer of fat known as dermal white adipose tissue.
assertions.quote: Dermal white adipose tissue is a unique layer of adipocytes within the reticular dermis of the skin.
assertions.note: Chen et al. define dermal white adipose tissue as a distinct layer of adipocytes within the reticular dermis.

assertions.text: In mice, dermal white adipose tissue expands rapidly following infection with Staphylococcus aureus.
assertions.quote: We observed rapid proliferation of preadipocytes and expansion of the dermal fat layer after infection of the skin by Staphylococcus aureus .
assertions.note: Zhang et al. observed rapid expansion of the dermal fat layer following cutaneous S. aureus infection in mice.

assertions.text: New adipocytes formed during this response in mice release the antimicrobial peptide cathelicidin.
assertions.quote: This host defense function was mediated through the production of cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide from adipocytes because cathelicidin expression was decreased by inhibition of adipogenesis, and adipocytes from Camp −/− mice lost the capacity to inhibit bacterial growth.
assertions.note: Zhang et al. confirmed that adipocytes provide host defense through the production of cathelicidin.

assertions.text: The capacity of dermal fat to mount this antimicrobial adipogenic response fades with age via TGF-beta signalling.
assertions.quote: Zhang et al. demonstrate that activation of the TGFβ pathway suppresses the adipogenic potential of dermal fibroblasts and therefore leads to an age-dependent loss of antimicrobial protection from dermal fat.
assertions.note: Zhang et al. (2019) demonstrated that age-dependent activation of the TGF-beta pathway impairs adipogenesis and antimicrobial defense.

assertions.text: Human skin arranges dermal white adipose tissue in cones surrounding hair follicles.
assertions.quote: In human skin, where all layers in the dermis have interfaces which run more or less parallel to the skin surface, dWAT is mainly concentrated around the pilosebaceous units that contain hair shafts, hair follicles, the sebaceous glands and the erector pili muscles, and the dWAT has a very special cone geometry (Figure I, panel C).
assertions.note: Kruglikov and Scherer describe dermal white adipose tissue in human skin forming cone-shaped geometry around pilosebaceous units.

assertions.text: Human acne lesions contain perifollicular preadipocytes that express cathelicidin.
assertions.quote: Perifollicular dermal preadipocytes in human acne and mouse skin lesions showed colocalization of PREF1, an early marker of adipogenesis, and cathelicidin ( Camp ), an antimicrobial peptide.
assertions.note: O'Neill et al. observed perifollicular preadipocytes expressing cathelicidin in human acne lesions.

assertions.text: What the dermal white adipose tissue layer contributes to human skin ageing has not been measured.
assertions.note: The provided sources describe age-related changes in dermal fat but do not state that its contribution to human skin ageing has not been measured.

recheck.note: None of the provided sources address whether the contribution of dermal white adipose tissue to human skin ageing has been measured.

assertions.note: The source identifies dermal white adipose tissue as a distinct fat depot from subcutaneous white adipose tissue.

Two fat layers, one follicle
Find the dermis, the two fat layers, and the follicle the thinner layer surrounds.
Dermal white adipose tissue
Hair follicle
Subcutaneous fat
Dermis

Human evidence
Fat that holds the face up.
Cadaver dissection shows that the face's subcutaneous fat sits in separate compartments, and facial ageing is partly how each compartment changes. Weight shows the same thing from the outside. In a study of 186 pairs of identical twins, the twin with the higher body-mass index looked older before about age 40 and younger after it.
pairs of identical twins compared for facial ageing
Guyuron et al., 2009 — a four-point higher BMI tracked with an older look before about 40 and a younger look after it
What it means: From midlife on, facial fat goes with a younger-looking face. That fits the anatomy: the face ages partly as its fat compartments change. GRADE C, observational.
What it does not mean: It is an observational comparison of photographs. It does not show that gaining weight rejuvenates, or that fat loss on a drug changes the skin itself.
units.sourceNote: Rohrich & Pessa 2007 · Guyuron 2009

assertions.text: Cadaver dissection shows that facial subcutaneous fat is partitioned into separate anatomical compartments, and facial aging is partly characterized by how these compartments change.
assertions.quote: The subcutaneous fat of the face is partitioned into discrete anatomic compartments. Facial aging is, in part, characterized by how these compartments change with age.
assertions.note: Rohrich and Pessa (2007) confirmed discrete subcutaneous fat compartments and their role in facial aging.

assertions.text: The Guyuron et al. (2009) study evaluated facial aging among 186 pairs of identical twins using questionnaires and digital images.
assertions.quote: During the Twins Day Festival in Twinsburg, Ohio, 186 pairs of identical twins completed a comprehensive questionnaire, and digital images were obtained.
assertions.note: Guyuron et al. obtained digital images and questionnaires from 186 pairs of identical twins.

assertions.text: A four-point higher body-mass index was associated with an older look before age 40 and a younger look after age 40.
assertions.quote: Four-point higher body mass index was associated with an older appearance in twins younger than age 40 but resulted in a younger appearance after age 40 (p = 0.0001).
assertions.note: The twin study found a 4-point higher BMI was associated with an older look under 40 and a younger look after 40.

units.text:
Mechanism
Sugar that sticks to collagen.
Glycation is a slow, non-enzymatic reaction. Reducing sugars attach to protein amino groups, rearrange into Amadori products and end as advanced glycation end products, or AGEs. On long-lived dermal collagen, AGEs form cross-links that stiffen the matrix. Through their receptor, RAGE, AGEs switch on inflammatory signalling in laboratory studies. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates the structural and inflammatory effects B; the course grades the causal link to visible ageing D, because the human data are associations.
Sugar + protein → Schiff base → Amadori product → AGE
Cross-links stiffen long-lived collagen
RAGE signalling: shown in the laboratory
Narration: Glycation is chemistry before it is biology. Reducing sugars attach to the amino groups of proteins, rearrange into more stable products, and end as advanced glycation end…
units.sourceNote: Gkogkolou & Böhm 2012 · Dyer 1993 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 13

assertions.text: Glycation is a non-enzymatic reaction in which reducing sugars attach to protein amino groups, forming a Schiff base that rearranges into Amadori products and culminates in advanced glycation end products (AGEs).
assertions.quote: Reducing sugars react non-enzymatically with protein amino groups to form a reversible Schiff base, then a more stable Amadori product, and finally irreversible advanced glycation end products (AGEs) — accelerated by hyperglycemia, a high-sugar or heavily processed diet, and UV exposure.[7]
assertions.note: The guide confirms the non-enzymatic reaction pathway from reducing sugars to Schiff bases, Amadori products, and AGEs.

assertions.text: On long-lived dermal collagen, AGEs form intermolecular cross-links that stiffen the extracellular matrix.
assertions.quote: Intermolecular crosslinks of adjacent collagen fibers change its biomechanical properties leading to stiffness and decreased flexibility, thus increasing its susceptibility to mechanical stimuli.
assertions.note: The review states that intermolecular cross-links formed on collagen fibers result in stiffness and decreased flexibility.

assertions.text: In laboratory studies, AGEs engage the RAGE receptor to switch on inflammatory signalling and enzymes that break down the matrix.
assertions.quote: In skin cells RAGE has been shown to decrease cell proliferation, induce apoptosis and increase MMPs production.
assertions.note: The review confirms that RAGE stimulation activates NF-κB and increases the production of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) in skin cells.

assertions.text: The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide assigns a Grade B rating to both the structural and inflammatory effects of AGEs.
assertions.quote: Structurally, they covalently cross-link long-lived collagen and elastin, stiffening the dermis and arterial wall and producing the loss of elasticity that reads as aged skin GRADE B. Biochemically, AGEs engage their receptor RAGE, driving NF-κB–mediated release of IL-6, TNF-α, and matrix metalloproteinases — a direct molecular link from metabolic load to inflammaging and matrix breakdown GRADE B.[7,8]
assertions.note: The guide explicitly assigns Grade B to both structural cross-linking and biochemical/inflammatory RAGE signaling.

assertions.text: The proposed causal link between AGEs and visible clinical skin ageing rests primarily on laboratory work, animal models, and correlational human data rather than controlled clinical outcome trials.
assertions.quote: As controlled human studies investigating the effects of these anti-AGE strategies against skin aging are largely missing, this is a hot field for future research.
assertions.note: The source notes that controlled human studies testing anti-AGE interventions against skin aging are largely missing.

assertions.text: Glycation proceeds sequentially from a reducing sugar binding a protein amino group to form a reversible Schiff base, followed by a more stable Amadori product, and ultimately irreversible advanced glycation end products (AGEs).
assertions.quote: Reducing sugars react non-enzymatically with protein amino groups to form a reversible Schiff base, then a more stable Amadori product, and finally irreversible advanced glycation end products (AGEs) — accelerated by hyperglycemia, a high-sugar or heavily processed diet, and UV exposure.[7]
assertions.note: The source explicitly describes this exact chemical sequence of glycation.

assertions.text: AGE cross-links stiffen long-lived collagen.

assertions.note: The source confirms that AGE cross-linking of long-lived collagen leads to matrix stiffening.

units.text:
Human evidence
Fifteen years on the same collagen.
Human skin collagen turns over slowly; tissue analysis puts its half-life at about 15 years. In skin biopsies, glycoxidation products in collagen rose about five-fold between ages 20 and 85, and were up to twice as high in type 1 diabetes. Skin autofluorescence, a non-invasive reading, correlates moderately with those biopsy measures and was validated in non-pigmented skin.
~15 years
estimated half-life of human skin collagen
Verzijl et al., 2000 · AGE content of skin collagen rises about five-fold from age 20 to 85 (Dyer et al., 1993)
What it means: Glycation damage accumulates on the same collagen for years, and faster with higher glucose exposure. That much is measured in human skin: direct, observational, GRADE C.
What it does not mean: It does not show how much of visible ageing AGEs cause, or that any product reverses established c…
units.sourceNote: Verzijl 2000 · Dyer 1993 · Meerwaldt 2004

assertions.text: Tissue analysis estimates the half-life of human skin collagen at about 15 years.
assertions.quote: From the age-related increases in % d-Asp the half-life of cartilage collagen was calculated to be 117 years and that of skin collagen 15 years, thereby providing the first reasonable estimates of the half-lives of these collagens.
assertions.note: Verzijl et al. calculated the half-life of human skin collagen to be 15 years from aspartic acid racemization.

assertions.text: In skin biopsies, glycoxidation products in collagen increased about five-fold between ages 20 and 85.
assertions.quote: In nondiabetic subjects, glycation ofcollagen (FL content) increased only 33% between 20 and 85 yrof age. In contrast, CML, pentosidine and fluorescence increased five- fold, correlating strongly with age.
assertions.note: Dyer et al. reported that CML, pentosidine, and fluorescence increased five-fold between ages 20 and 85.

assertions.text: Skin collagen glycoxidation products were up to twice as high in type 1 diabetes compared with controls.
assertions.quote: Collagen CML, pentosidine and fluorescence were increased up to twofold in diabetic compared with control pa- tients: this could be explained by the increase in glycation alone, without invoking increased oxidative stress.
assertions.note: Dyer et al. reported that collagen CML, pentosidine, and fluorescence were increased up to twofold in diabetic patients.

assertions.text: Skin autofluorescence correlates moderately with skin biopsy measures of collagen advanced glycation end products.
assertions.quote: Autofluorescence correlated with CLF, pentosidine, CML, and CEL ( r=0.47-0.62, p</=0.002).
assertions.note: Meerwaldt et al. found that skin autofluorescence correlated moderately with biopsy AGE measures (r = 0.47 to 0.62).

assertions.text: Skin autofluorescence measurement has been validated in non-pigmented skin.
assertions.quote: The AFR offers a simple alternative to invasive measurement of AGE accumulation and, to date, has been validated in non-pigmented skin.
assertions.note: Meerwaldt et al. note that the autofluorescence reader had been validated in non-pigmented skin.

units.text:
Lesson 3.2 · Concept
Two gut hormones, re-engineered.
GLP-1 and GIP are incretins, hormones the gut releases after a meal that amplify glucose-dependent insulin release; GLP-1 also slows gastric emptying and reduces appetite. Native GLP-1 is broken down within minutes. Semaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist, and tirzepatide activates both GIP and GLP-1 receptors. In the US, as of September 2026, both are FDA-approved drugs for defined indications, set out in the next moment.
Incretins amplify insulin after meals
Semaglutide: GLP-1 receptor agonist
Tirzepatide: GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist
Narration: After a meal, the gut releases two hormones called incretins, GLP-1 and GIP. Both amplify insulin release when glucose is high, and GLP-1 also slows the stomach and reduces appetite. Native GLP-1 lasts only minutes in the blood before an enzyme breaks it down, so the drug molec…

units.text:
Regulatory status
Approved for what, exactly?
The facial changes in this lesson happen to people taking approved drugs for approved reasons. Know the indications, and their dates, before you discuss the side effects. Status below is for the US, from FDA records checked in September 2026.
Ozempic (semaglutide)
Type 2 diabetes
First approved 2017. The label adds cardiovascular and kidney risk reduction in people with type 2 diabetes.
Wegovy (semaglutide)
Chronic weight management
Approved June 2021; adolescents from age 12 added December 2022. Cardiovascular risk reduction in established heart disease with obesity or overweight, March 2024. MASH with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis, accelerated approval, August 2025.
Mounjaro (tirzepatide)
First approved 2022. The label adds cardiovascular risk reduction in type 2 diabetes at high risk.
Zepbound (tirzepatide)
Approved November 2023. Mo…

units.text:
Human evidence
Large trials, measured on the scale.
In STEP-1, 1,961 adults without diabetes lost a mean 14.9% of body weight on semaglutide over 68 weeks, against 2.4% on placebo. In SURMOUNT-1, 2,539 adults lost 15.0% to 20.9% on tirzepatide over 72 weeks, depending on dose, against 3.1% on placebo. Both Hormonaly guides grade weight management A. Across 35 randomized trials of incretin drugs, a median of about 28% of the weight lost was muscle-related tissue.
14.9% · 20.9%
mean weight loss in STEP-1 (semaglutide, 68 weeks) and SURMOUNT-1 (tirzepatide, highest dose, 72 weeks)
Placebo 2.4% and 3.1% · both trials industry-funded, both the basis for approval
What it means: These drugs produce large, reproducible weight loss in randomized trials: GRADE A for the approved indications. Part of what is lost is lean tissue, which is why the Hormonaly guide pairs treatment with protein and resi…

units.text:
Four registers
'Ozempic face', answer by answer.
The phrase bundles four kinds of statement. Kept apart, they tell a patient far more than the headline does.
Mechanism
Volume loss
Losing fat deflates the superficial facial compartments and unmasks laxity that was already there.
Human evidence
Observational and small: C to D
One imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial, about 7% per 10 kg lost. A survey of 1,226 patients found sagging, facial volume loss and hair shedding reported more often the more weight was lost. A systematic review of the plastic-surgery literature found it limited by study bias. No randomized trial has measured the face.
Regulatory status (US, September 2026)
Hair loss labelled; facial change unlisted
Both labels list hair loss (about 3–6% on drug against about 1% on placebo, mostly in women, linked to weight reductio…
units.sourceNote: Sharma 2025 · Rao 2026 · Daneshgaran 2025 · US labels 2026 · Paschou 2025

assertions.text: Losing fat deflates the superficial facial compartments and unmasks laxity that was already there.
assertions.quote: Rapid, large-volume weight loss strips subcutaneous fat from the face, producing the hollowed, prematurely aged look popularly called "Ozempic face" — a volume change rather than accelerated skin aging, though it unmasks pre-existing laxity; restoration (filler, fat grafting, energy-based tightening) is the usual remedy.[7]

assertions.text: One imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial.

What changes in practice
Counsel before, record during, refer when asked.
Raise facial volume change and hair shedding before treatment starts; the Hormonaly guide advises this especially for older patients. During treatment, photograph the face with consent, and support the protein intake and resistance training the guide recommends to protect lean mass. When a patient wants the face restored, refer to a qualified aesthetic or dermatology colleague. Published advice on restoration is expert opinion, the main consensus statement was developed with industry involvement, and randomized trials of fillers and devices in these patients are registered without results. Decisions about the medicine itself stay with the prescriber and the patient.

units.text:
Lesson 3.3 · Concept
Inflammation that comes with age.
Inflammaging is the chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that rises with age. In older adults, higher IL-6 and CRP predict frailty and death. One proposed source is the gut. In mice, a high-fat diet raises circulating bacterial lipopolysaccharide, and infusing it reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance. In 12 healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised plasma endotoxin within four hours. Whether a leaky gut drives skin disease in people has not been shown.
Inflammaging: low-grade, sterile, age-related
Metabolic endotoxaemia: gut bacterial LPS in the blood
Gut to skin in people: not shown
Narration: Ageing brings a slow rise in background inflammation, called inflammaging. It is low-grade and sterile, and in older adults higher IL-6 and C-reactive protein predict frailty, disability and death. One proposed source is the gut. …

assertions.text: Inflammaging is the chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that rises with age.
assertions.quote: Inflammaging is the chronic, sterile, low-grade inflammation that accumulates with age and predicts frailty, multimorbidity, and mortality.

assertions.note: The clinical summary confirms elevated IL-6 and CRP independently predict mortality, frailty, and disability in older adults.

assertions.text: In mice, a high-fat diet raises circulating bacterial lipopolysaccharide, and infusing it reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance.
assertions.quote: When metabolic endotoxemia was induced for 4 weeks in mice through continuous subcutaneous infusion of LPS, fasted glycemia and insulinemia and whole-body, liver, and adipose tissue weight gain were increased to a similar extent as in high-fat-fed mice.
assertions.note: The mouse study found high-fat diet elevated plasma LPS and 4-week LPS infusion reproduced weight gain and liver insulin resistance.

assertions.text: In 12 healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised plasma endotoxin within four hours.
assertions.quote: Plasma endotoxin and endotoxin neutralization capacity were measured for 4 h in 12 healthy men after no meal, 3 cigarettes, a high-fat meal, or a high-fat meal with 3 cigarettes by using the limulus assay. A 2024 European task-force meta-analysis in children without food allergy reported a significant fall in severity scores.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Diet first, a bottle last.
When a patient links their skin to their gut, start with what has evidence: diet quality, treating metabolic disease directly, and established treatment for the skin condition itself. A widely used commercial zonulin assay has been shown to detect proteins other than zonulin, so a result cannot tell you whether a gut is leaky. Restoring barrier function has not been shown to improve disease outside the gut. Investigational peptides sold for gut repair come last, if at all.
Start with diet, metabolic health and the skin diagnosis
Zonulin tests may not measure zonulin
Gut-repair peptides: last, if at all
Narration: Patients often link their skin to their gut. Start where the evidence is. Diet quality, treatment of metabolic disease and the established treatment for the skin condition itself all come first. Be careful with tests. A widely …

units.text:
Where does the page overreach?
A patient shows you this fictional sales page for a 'gut–skin reset' kit. Which sentences does the evidence not support?
Sound line: Background inflammation rises slowly with age; researchers call it inflammaging.
Explanation: Supported. Inflammaging is the chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that rises with age.
Sound line: In older adults, higher IL-6 and CRP predict frailty and death.
Explanation: Supported, as a prediction: in older adults, higher IL-6 and CRP predict frailty, disability and death.
Flagged line (the learner flags it; the course's claim is only that the evidence does not support it): "Studies show that a high-fat diet raises gut bacterial toxin in the blood, and that the toxin causes weight gain and insulin resistance."
Explanation: Shown in mice. There, a high-fat diet raised bacterial lipopolysaccharide in the blood, and infusing …

assertions.text: Background inflammation rises slowly with age, a phenomenon termed inflammaging.
assertions.quote: Inflammageing, defined as an age-related increase in the levels of pro-inflammatory markers in blood and tissues, is a strong risk factor for multiple diseases that are highly prevalent and frequent causes of disability in elderly individuals but are pathophysiologically uncorrelated.
assertions.note: Inflammaging is explicitly described as an age-related increase in pro-inflammatory markers.

assertions.text: In older adults, higher IL-6 and CRP levels predict frailty and death.
assertions.quote: elevated levels independently predict mortality, frailty, and disability in older adults.
assertions.note: The guide notes that elevated IL-6 and CRP independently predict frailty, disability, and mortality.

assertions.text: The evidence does not support the unqualified claim that a high-fat diet causes bacterial endotoxin to raise in the blood and drive weight gain and insulin resistance in humans, as this mechanism was demonstrated in mice.
assertions.quote: When metabolic endotoxemia was induced for 4 weeks in mice through continuous subcutaneous infusion of LPS, fasted glycemia and insulinemia and whole-body, liver, and adipose tissue weight gain were increased to a similar extent as in high-fat-fed mice.
assertions.note: The study establishing metabolic endotoxemia driving weight gain and insulin resistance was conducted in mice.

assertions.text: In a study of 12 healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised blood endotoxin concentrations within 4 hours.
assertions.quote: Baseline endotoxin concentrations were 8.2 pg/mL (interquartile range: 3.4-13.5 pg/mL) but increased significantly (P < 0.05) by approximately 50% after a high-fat meal or after a high-fat meal with cigarettes but not after no meal or cigarettes alone.
assertions.note: Erridge et al. observed this 50% increase in endotoxin across 4 hours in 12 healthy men.

assertions.text: The evidence does not support the claim that gut barrier leakage drives skin diseases like acne, eczema, and rosacea.
assertions.quote: Several other non-gastrointestinal diseases have been associated with leaky gut, based on limited or no supporting data, including asthma, autism, Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis, eczema, psoriasis, eosinophilic esophagitis, environmental enteropathy, kwashiorkor, fibromyalgia, depression, chronic fatigue syndrome, multi-organ failure syndrome (shock, burns, trauma), non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), alcoholic cirrhosis, obesity, metabolic syndrome, pancreatitis, and rheumatoid arthritis.
assertions.note: Camilleri notes that non-gastrointestinal diseases like eczema are associated with leaky gut based on limited or no supporting data.

assertions.text: The evidence does not support the claim that sealing the intestinal barrier clears skin conditions or improves extra-intestinal disease.
assertions.quote: It is still unproven that restoring barrier function can ameliorate clinical manifestations in gastrointestinal or systemic diseases.
assertions.note: Camilleri explicitly notes it remains unproven that restoring barrier function ameliorates clinical manifestations outside the gut.

assertions.text: A fibre-rich diet has strong evidence for cardiovascular and metabolic health.
assertions.quote: Dietary fiber and minimally processed, plant-rich eating consistently improve metabolic and inflammatory markers and feed short-chain-fatty-acid–producing microbes that support the barrier GRADE A.[1]
assertions.note: The guide assigns Grade A evidence to dietary fiber for metabolic and barrier health, supported by reviews showing reduced cardiovascular and metabolic outcomes.

units.text:
A patient asks for a zonulin blood test to prove that her rosacea comes from a leaky gut. What is the most accurate reply?
Explanation: Ask what a test measures before you ask what it shows.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The test will show whether her gut barrier is causing the rosacea.
Explanation: A widely used zonulin assay detects other proteins, and a zonulin result cannot tell you what is causing her rosacea.
Correct answer: The test is unreliable and would not change care: treat the rosacea on its own evidence, and assess any gut symptoms clinically.
Explanation: Correct. The small trial that linked gut bacteria to rosacea used breath testing and clinical assessment, and no zonulin test.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Rosacea has nothing to do with the gut, so there is nothing to discuss.
Explanation: Too strong: a small randomized trial found rosace…

assertions.text: A widely used zonulin assay detects other proteins rather than zonulin.
assertions.quote: We found that the ELISA kit used in the present study does not detect purified pre-HP2 but rather targets one or more proteins from a range of candidate molecules possibly structurally and functionally related to zonulin.
assertions.note: A study investigating the widely used commercial ELISA kit demonstrated that it does not detect pre-haptoglobin2 but targets other proteins.

assertions.text: The trial investigating the link between gut bacteria and rosacea evaluated patients with breath tests and clinical assessment, not a zonulin test.
assertions.quote: Patients and controls underwent lactulose and glucose breath tests (BTs) to assess the presence of SIBO.
assertions.note: The clinical trial used lactulose and glucose breath tests and dermatologic examinations rather than zonulin testing.

assertions.text: A randomized trial found that rosacea improved after small intestinal bacterial overgrowth was eradicated.
assertions.quote: After eradication, cutaneous lesions cleared in 20 of 28 and greatly improved in 6 of 28 patients, whereas patients treated with placebo remained unchanged (18/20) or worsened (2/20) (P < .001).
assertions.note: Rifaximin treatment leading to SIBO eradication led to complete clearance or substantial improvement in cutaneous lesions compared to placebo.

A plasma tripeptide with a copper habit.
GHK is a tripeptide found in human plasma, first described in 1973. Bound to copper it becomes GHK-Cu, which is proposed to deliver copper to enzymes such as superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase and to switch on wound-healing and antioxidant gene programmes. Most of that mechanistic literature comes from the group that discovered the peptide.

Proposed: copper delivery to matrix and antioxidant enzymes

It binds copper readily, and the copper complex, GHK-Cu, is what skin-care labels mean when they say copper peptide. The proposed mechanism is that GHK-Cu delivers copper to enzymes that build and protect…

Human evidence
One indexed randomized trial.
A search of PubMed in September 2026 found one randomized controlled trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin: 2006, healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing. The cosmetic trials cited for anti-ageing claims are manufacturer-sponsored and not indexed. Both Hormonaly guides grade topical use C.

indexed randomized trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin
Miller et al., 2006 — healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing, not photoageing
What it means: The human evidence for topical GHK-Cu is small: one small indexed trial plus sponsor-run cosmetic studies. GRADE C is the honest ceiling.
What it does not mean: It does not show that GHK-Cu fails, that it treats photoageing, or anything about injecting it. A thin evidence base is an unknown, not a negative.

Serum yes, syringe no.

Injectable: anecdote, common local reactions
Say which route you mean every time

units.text:
Lesson 4.2 · Concept
Three families, one question: who ran the trial?
Signal peptides such as palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) are meant to tell fibroblasts to make matrix. SNAP-25 mimics (Argireline and its longer cousin SNAP-8) and Leuphasyl, an enkephalin analogue, are meant to quieten expression lines. Oral collagen peptides are swallowed, not applied. All three families have a trial record, and in all three the question that matters most is who funded it.
Signal peptides: 'make more matrix'
SNAP-25 mimics: 'relax the line'
Oral collagen: the supplement aisle
Narration: Lesson two covers three families that fill the cosmetic and supplement shelves. Signal peptides, like palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, sold as Matrixyl, are fragments of matrix proteins meant to tell fibroblasts to make more collagen. SNAP-25 mimics, Argireline and its longer cousin SNAP-8, copy part of a nerve…

assertions.text: Signal peptides such as palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) are fragments of matrix proteins meant to stimulate fibroblasts to produce matrix and collagen.
assertions.quote: Matrixyl ® is the new version of Pentapeptide-4 (palmitoylated Lys-Thr-Thr-Lys-Ser-OH), the well-known signal peptide fragment of the C-terminal propeptide of type I collagen. It stimulates feedback regulation of new collagen synthesis and ECM proteins.
assertions.note: Errante et al. describe Matrixyl as a signal peptide fragment of type I collagen that stimulates new collagen and ECM protein synthesis.

assertions.text: SNAP-25 mimics such as Argireline and SNAP-8 copy part of SNAP-25, the nerve-terminal protein targeted by botulinum toxin, to help soften or quieten expression lines.
assertions.quote: The sequence Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-NH 2 (Blanes-Mira et al., 2002 ), covers the N-terminal fragment domain of SNAP-25, promoting the inhibition of Ca 2+ -dependent catecholamine release through the interrupted formation of SNARE complex. In comparison to the botulinum toxin, Argireline presents similar potency but lower efficacy.
assertions.note: Errante et al. confirm that Argireline covers a fragment domain of SNAP-25 and acts as a safe alternative to botulinum toxin to diminish wrinkles.

assertions.text: Leuphasyl is an enkephalin analogue meant to quieten expression lines and reduce wrinkles.
assertions.quote: It acts like enkephalins, decreasing the ACh secretion in the synaptic cleft. Both instrumental and volunteer-involving studies acknowledge its effectiveness in wrinkles reduction (Dragomirescu et al., 2014 ).
assertions.note: Errante et al. describe Leuphasyl as acting like enkephalins to reduce wrinkles.

The evidence
Twenty-three trials, split by who paid.
Pooled, oral collagen trials show better hydration, elasticity and wrinkle scores, and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades them C. A 2025 meta-analysis split the same kind of trials by funding and by quality. The benefit appeared only in pharmaceutical-funded and low-quality trials. Unfunded and high-quality trials showed no effect.
23 RCTs
in the 2025 meta-analysis that split oral-collagen trials by funding and quality
1,474 participants
What it means: The pooled benefit of oral collagen disappears when you look only at independent or high-quality trials. The course keeps the guide's GRADE C and shows why a downgrade has been proposed to its author.
What it does not mean: It does not show collagen is harmful, and it does not rule out benefit for an individual. It is a statement about the evidence, and it says nothi…

Cosmetic, supplement, drug: three rulebooks.
In the US, cosmetic peptides are cosmetic ingredients, not drugs, and their safety is assessed under a cosmetics framework. Oral collagen is a dietary supplement: it may not claim to treat disease, and product quality and content vary. Neither route has to prove efficacy before sale — which is why the funding question matters.
Cosmetic ingredient: no efficacy approval needed
Dietary supplement: no disease claims; quality varies

units.text:
A patient shows you a collagen drink labelled 'clinically proven to reduce wrinkles'. What is the most accurate reply?
Explanation: Ask who paid for the trial before you ask what it showed.
Correct answer: The trials are real, but the benefit shows up only in industry-funded and lower-quality trials; independent, high-quality trials show no effect.
Explanation: Correct. That is what the 2025 funding-stratified meta-analysis found.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Meta-analyses prove that collagen improves skin.
Explanation: Pooled, yes. Split by funding and quality, the effect disappears in the independent and high-quality trials.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Collagen is digested, so it cannot do anything.
Explanation: That is a mechanism argument. The course rests on the trials, and the problem with the trials is who ran them.

assertions.text: When pooled without stratification, meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials shows that collagen supplements significantly improve skin aging parameters.
assertions.quote: In a meta-analysis of all 23 RCTs, collagen supplements significantly improved skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles.
assertions.note: Supported by the 2025 meta-analysis of all 23 RCTs.

assertions.text: In subgroup meta-analysis by funding source, independent trials not funded by pharmaceutical companies show no effect of collagen supplements, while industry-funded trials show significant effects.
assertions.quote: However, in the subgroup meta-analysis by funding source, studies not receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies revealed no effect of collagen supplements for improving skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles, while those receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies did show significant effects.
assertions.note: Supported by the 2025 funding-stratified meta-analysis.

assertions.text: In subgroup meta-analysis by study quality, high-quality trials reveal no significant effect of collagen supplements across categories, whereas lower-quality trials show significant improvement.
assertions.quote: Similarly, high-quality studies revealed no significant effect in all categories, while low-quality studies revealed a significant improvement in elasticity.
assertions.note: Supported by the quality subgroup analysis in the 2025 meta-analysis.

Lesson 4.3 · Concept
Rodents, a fragment, and a tripeptide.
BPC-157 rests on a large rodent literature, mostly from one research group, and on uncontrolled human case series. TB-500 is not thymosin β4: it is a seven-residue fragment of it, identified by analysing the product itself, and no trial has tested the fragment. KPV, a tripeptide from the end of α-MSH, calms inflammation in mouse colitis and has no randomized human trial.
BPC-157: rodents and case series
TB-500: a fragment, never trialled
KPV: mouse colitis only

Its evidence is a large rodent literature, most of it from one research group, and uncontrolled human case series. units.text:
The evidence
One abstract, no published trial.
As of September 2026 no randomized efficacy trial of BPC-157 in people has been published in full. FDA's July 2026 briefing found one randomized, placebo-controlled trial reported only as a 2005 meeting abstract: 53 people with ulcerative colitis, two weeks of treatment, and no significant difference from placebo. ClinicalTrials.gov adds a 2015 phase 1 safety study that never posted results, a completed 2025 single-arm product study with no results posted, and a randomized phase 1 trial after rotator-cuff surgery due to start in 2027.

One 2005 ulcerative-colitis trial exists only as a meeting abstract (no significant difference from placebo) · registered: phase 1 safety study (2015, no results) · single-arm product study (2025, no results) · randomized phase 1…

units.text:
Worked example
Two trials, one peptide: LL-37.
LL-37, the skin's own cathelicidin, is the one repair peptide with two randomized trials in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers. Read them in order.
First trial (2014)
Positive at low dose
First-in-human, randomized, dose-ranging; 34 patients
Second trial (2021)
Negative in the full cohort
Multicentre phase IIb, placebo-controlled; only a post hoc subgroup signal
Who ran them
The developer, both times
Sponsorship does not make a trial wrong; it is one more reason to wait for replication
Grade
C — inconsistent
A small positive trial followed by an adequately powered negative one
Callout: A small positive trial is a hypothesis. LL-37 is what happens when someone tests it.
units.sourceNote: Grönberg 2014 · Mahlapuu 2021 · Schauber & Gallo 2008

assertions.text: LL-37 is an endogenous cathelicidin peptide of the skin.
assertions.quote: Cathelicidins are unique AMPs that protect the skin through 2 distinct pathways: (1) direct antimicrobial activity and (2) initiation of a host response resulting in cytokine release, inflammation, angiogenesis, and reepithelialization.
assertions.note: Schauber & Gallo (2008) describes cutaneous cathelicidins as antimicrobial peptides protecting the skin.

assertions.text: LL-37 is the only repair peptide with two randomized trials in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers.
assertions.quote: Two randomized placebo-controlled trials have evaluated topical LL-37 in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers.
assertions.note: The sources confirm that LL-37 has two randomized trials in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers, but do not show that it is the only repair peptide with two such trials.

recheck.note: The sources confirm that LL-37 has two randomized trials in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers, but do not show that it is the only repair peptide with two such trials.

assertions.text: The first trial (2014) of LL-37 in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers was a first-in-human, randomized, dose-ranging study of 34 patients that was positive at low dose.
assertions.quote: This first-in-man trial included 34 participants with VLUs and comprised a 3-week, open-label, run-in period on placebo, followed by a 4-week randomized double-blind treatment phase with twice weekly applications of LL-37 (0.5, 1.6, or 3.2 mg/mL) or placebo, and a 4-week follow-up.
assertions.note: Grönberg 2014 describes this 34-patient first-in-man trial demonstrating improved healing at the two lower doses.

assertions.text: The second trial (2021) of LL-37 was a multicentre phase IIb placebo-controlled study that was negative in the full cohort, showing only a post hoc subgroup signal.
assertions.quote: Efficacy analysis performed on the full study population did not identify any significant improvement in healing in patients treated with LL‐37 as compared with the placebo. In contrast, a post hoc analysis revealed statistically significant improvement with LL‐37 treatment in several interrelated healing parameters in the subgroup of patients with large target wounds (a wound area of at least 10 cm2 at randomization), which is a known negative prognostic factor for healing.
assertions.note: Mahlapuu 2021 confirms that the full-cohort efficacy analysis showed no significant healing improvement, with positive signals found only on post hoc subgroup analysis.

assertions.text: Both clinical trials of LL-37 were run by the developer.

assertions.text: For GHK-Cu injection, evidence is limited to anecdotes or case series without randomized trials, and local reactions are common because copper irritates tissue.

units.text: If you practise in the UK, the route for unlicensed medicines works differently, and lesson 7.2 sets it out.

In the EU, a medicine prepared in a pharmacy on prescription for an individual patient (magistral formula), or to a pharmacopoeia for the pharmacy's own patients (officinal formula), falls outside Directive 2001/83/EC and needs no marketing authorisation under it (Article 3), and each member state may, under its own law, allow an unauthorised medicine for an individual patient on a professional's bona fide unsolicited order, under that professional's direct personal responsibility (Article 5(1)). No centrally authorised medicine containing GHK-Cu, BPC-157 or TB-500 was found in the Union Register or in EMA's data on authorised, refused and withdrawn medicines (searched 25 September 2026).

assertions.quote:
This Directive shall not apply to:

1. 

Any medicinal product prepared in a pharmacy in accordance with a medical prescription for an individual patient (commonly known as the magistral formula).
assertions.note: Article 3 excludes both magistral and officinal formulas prepared in a pharmacy from the scope of Directive 2001/83/EC.

assertions.text: Each EU member state may, under its own law, allow an unauthorised medicine for an individual patient on a professional's bona fide unsolicited order, under that professional's direct personal responsibility (Article 5(1)).

assertions.note: Article 5(1) permits member states to exclude from the directive products supplied in response to a bona fide unsolicited order for an individual patient under an authorised professional's direct personal responsibility.

units.text: In Portugal, a magistral formula is a medicine prepared in a community or hospital pharmacy, under a pharmacist's responsibility, on a medical prescription that names the patient, and the prescribing physician must satisfy themselves of its safety and efficacy (Decreto-Lei 95/2004). Compounded medicines may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese pharmacopoeia, the European pharmacopoeia or another European pharmacopoeia, or in compendial scientific documentation, and one containing any other raw material may not be prescribed.

units.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that any substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded, and that compounding may only be individual, on presentation of a medical prescription, by a compounding pharmacy licensed by local health surveillance. units.text: In the UAE, the medicines law (Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024, in force 2 January 2025) exempts medical products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies from the requirement for a marketing approval from the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE). units.text:
Fictional case
New dark patches, three months into 'GLOW'.
A 46-year-old patient has been injecting a research-use-only 'GLOW' blend bought online for three months. She reports smoother skin and asks about continuing. You notice new, patchy darkening on her face and forearms. This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence; there is one right first move.
Role version (prescriber): You assess the pigmentation or refer to dermatology, consider whether investigation is needed, and document the investigational product and your advice.
Role version (clinical-staff): You record the product, source and batch, photograph with consent if your setting allows, and escalate to the prescriber the same day.
Role version (advisor): You advise her to stop, keep the vial and packaging, and see a prescriber promptly; you do not suggest an alternative supplier.
Narration: A fictional case, built …

units.sourceNote: Ito 2005 · Horesh 2023 · Bertolini 2020 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 6

units.text:
Mechanism
A follicle that runs its own hormones.
Human scalp hair follicles kept alive in the laboratory answer corticotropin-releasing hormone by making ACTH and α-MSH and secreting cortisol, with a feedback loop like the adrenal axis. They also run a growth hormone and IGF-1 loop of their own. Locally made dihydrotestosterone shrinks genetically susceptible scalp follicles, the process behind pattern hair loss. Growing follicles are shielded from immune attack, and alopecia areata begins when that shield fails.
Local stress axis: CRH → ACTH → cortisol, with feedback
Local androgen switch: testosterone → DHT in the scalp
Immune privilege: its collapse drives alopecia areata
Narration: Each hair follicle behaves like a small gland. When researchers keep human scalp follicles alive in culture, the follicles answer corticotropin-releasing hormone the way the pituitary and adrenal glands do…
units.sourceNote: Ito 2005 · Horesh 2023 · Bertolini 2020 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 6

assertions.text: Human scalp hair follicles kept alive in culture respond to corticotropin-releasing hormone by producing ACTH and α-MSH, secreting cortisol, and displaying an adrenal-like feedback loop.
assertions.quote: Thus, even in the absence of endocrine, neural, or vascular systemic connections, normal human scalp hair follicles directly respond to CRH stimulation in a strikingly similar manner to what is seen in the classical HPA axis, including synthesis and secretion of cortisol and activation of prototypic neuroendocrine feedback loops.
assertions.note: The abstract confirms that organ-cultured human scalp hair follicles synthesize ACTH, α-MSH, and cortisol in response to CRH and display feedback downregulation by hydrocortisone.

assertions.text: Hair follicles operate an autonomous growth hormone and IGF-1 loop of their own.
assertions.quote: The human hair follicle runs functional peripheral equivalents of the central axes: it synthesizes cortisol and operates a local HPA-like loop,[11] and ex vivo it sustains a hypothalamic–pituitary–somatotropic equivalent (GHRH, GH, IGF-1) that paces its own growth.[12]
assertions.note: The textbook excerpt confirms that human hair follicles sustain an ex vivo hypothalamic-pituitary-somatotropic equivalent including GH and IGF-1.

assertions.text: In the scalp, 5α-reductase converts testosterone into dihydrotestosterone, which miniaturizes genetically susceptible follicles to drive pattern hair loss.
assertions.quote: Thyroid hormone and prolactin tune the cycle and estrogen withdrawal at menopause thins hair, but the dominant clinical lever is androgenic: 5α-reductase converts testosterone to DHT, which paradoxically miniaturizes genetically susceptible scalp follicles (androgenetic alopecia) while driving beard and body hair.
assertions.note: The text confirms that 5α-reductase converts testosterone to DHT, which miniaturizes genetically susceptible follicles in androgenetic alopecia.

assertions.text: Growing hair follicles are protected by immune privilege, and the collapse of this protection leads to immune attack resulting in alopecia areata.
assertions.quote: Collapse of anagen hair bulb IP is an essential prerequisite for the development of alopecia areata (AA).
assertions.note: The review states that collapse of anagen hair bulb immune privilege is an essential prerequisite for alopecia areata development.

units.text:
Human evidence
Two trials, 1,200 adults, one approval.
When immune privilege fails, the attack depends on cytokine signals that JAK inhibitors interrupt. Two randomized phase 3 trials tested oral baricitinib in 1,200 adults with severe alopecia areata. In the US, FDA approved baricitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades it A.
adults with severe alopecia areata in the two phase 3 trials of baricitinib (2022)
At 36 weeks, up to 39% of patients on baricitinib had at least 80% of their scalp hair, against 3–6% on placebo
What it means: Interrupting the immune signalling behind collapsed privilege regrows hair in severe alopecia areata. That is approval-grade evidence (A), and it shows what real follicle evidence looks like.
What it does not mean: It says nothing about pattern hair loss, cosmetic thinning or any pe…
units.sourceNote: King 2022 (BRAVE-AA1 and -AA2) · FDA approval letter, 13 Jun 2022

assertions.quote: It is also an immune-privileged site — normally shielded from immune attack — and collapse of that privilege drives alopecia areata, now treatable with JAK inhibitors that interrupt the responsible cytokine signaling (oral baricitinib is approved for severe disease GRADE A).[13]
assertions.note: The guide notes that hair follicle immune privilege collapse drives alopecia areata, which is treatable with JAK inhibitors that interrupt cytokine signaling.

APPROVAL & LABELING We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.

units.text: In the EU, baricitinib (Olumiant) has been centrally authorised since 13 February 2017; its indications include severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over, and it is prescription-only, started by a doctor experienced in the condition (EMA). Work up the hair loss before anyone mentions a peptide.

A 32-year-old woman asks for a compounded peptide scalp spray. Diffuse shedding began three months after she gave birth; there are no patches and no signs of androgen excess. What comes first?

units.text:
Lesson 5.2 · Concept
Five receptors, one family of hormones.
Skin makes proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and cuts it into ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. Those peptides act on five melanocortin receptors. MC1R drives pigment in skin and hair, MC2R answers ACTH in the adrenal gland, MC3R and MC4R act in the brain on appetite, and MC5R governs sebum. Which receptors a drug reaches decides what else it does.
MC1R: pigment of skin and hair
MC2R: adrenal · MC5R: sebum
MC3R and MC4R: appetite, in the brain
Narration: Pigment starts with hormones the skin makes for itself. Skin cells produce a precursor called POMC and cut it into ACTH, alpha-MSH and beta-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. There are five melanocortin receptors. MC1R sets the pigment of skin and hair. MC2R is the adrenal receptor for ACTH. MC3R and …

assertions.text: The skin produces POMC and cleaves it into ACTH, α-MSH, and β-endorphin, and the same cells express the receptors that respond to them.
assertions.quote: In fact, all of the elements controlling the activity of the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal axis are expressed in the skin including CRH, urocortin, and POMC, with its products ACTH, alpha-MSH, and beta-endorphin. Demonstration of the corresponding receptors in the same cells suggests para- or autocrine mechanisms of action.
assertions.note: Supported by the review of cutaneous neuroendocrinology.

assertions.text: There are five melanocortin receptors.
assertions.quote: The 5 known melanocortin receptors (MCs) have established physiological roles.
assertions.note: Supported by the review of the melanocortin receptor family.

assertions.text: MC1R drives pigmentation in skin and hair.
assertions.quote: MC1 mediates pigmentation of both skin and hair, MC2 is required for adrenal steroidogenesis and therefore the stress response, MC3 and MC4 modulate the central control of food intake and satiety, and MC5 regulates sebogenesis.
assertions.note: Supported by the description of established physiological roles.

assertions.text: MC2R responds to ACTH in the adrenal gland.
assertions.quote: MC2R, expressed in the adrenal cortex, is involved in steroidogenesis. Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) binds to MC2R located on the surface of adrenal zona fasciculata cells, thereby producing cortisol.
assertions.note: Supported by the review describing MC2R location and function.

assertions.text: MC3R and MC4R act centrally to regulate appetite.
assertions.quote: MC3 and MC4 modulate the central control of food intake and satiety, and MC5 regulates sebogenesis.
assertions.note: Supported by the text noting MC3 and MC4 modulate central control of food intake.

assertions.text: Central melanocortin receptors also influence sexual responses.
assertions.quote: Some studies have reported the association between MC4R and sexual function.
assertions.note: Supported by the association between central MC4R and sexual function.

assertions.text: MC5R regulates sebum production.
assertions.quote: MC5 regulates sebogenesis.
assertions.note: Supported by the description of MC5 function.

Pigment, adrenal, brain, sebum
Those peptides act on five melanocortin receptors, and which receptors a drug reaches decides what else it does.

assertions.text: Melanocortin peptides act on five melanocortin receptors, governing functions in pigmentation, the adrenal gland, the brain, and sebum production.
assertions.quote: MC1 mediates pigmentation of both skin and hair, MC2 is required for adrenal steroidogenesis and therefore the stress response, MC3 and MC4 modulate the central control of food intake and satiety, and MC5 regulates sebogenesis.
assertions.note: The source identifies the five melanocortin receptors and their respective roles in pigmentation, adrenal steroidogenesis, central satiety/food intake, and sebogenesis.

assertions.text: Which melanocortin receptors a drug reaches determines what additional effects it produces.
assertions.quote: Because melanotan II can cross the blood–brain barrier and is nonselective, it also activates the other MCRs, resulting in adverse events including fatigue, loss of appetite and penile erection.
assertions.note: The source demonstrates that a drug's receptor selectivity profile across the melanocortin receptors dictates its other physiological and adverse effects.

Five melanocortin receptors do four jobs. Find each job on the tiles.

assertions.text: MC2R is an adrenal receptor for ACTH.
assertions.quote: MC2R, expressed in the adrenal cortex, is involved in steroidogenesis. Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) binds to MC2R located on the surface of adrenal zona fasciculata cells, thereby producing cortisol.

units.text:
Four registers
One receptor family, two very different molecules.
Afamelanotide and Melanotan II are both synthetic relatives of α-MSH. Compare them register by register and the resemblance ends at the receptor.
Mechanism
Afamelanotide: MC1R agonist · Melanotan II: non-selective
Melanotan II also acts on MC3R, MC4R and MC5R and reaches the brain
Human evidence
Afamelanotide: A, for EPP only · Melanotan II: D
Two phase 3 trials in erythropoietic protoporphyria, against a three-volunteer pilot and a ten-man erectile-dysfunction study from the 1990s. The Peptide Pocket Guide rates Melanotan II C and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide D; with no trial of tanning, this course uses D.
Regulatory status
Afamelanotide: EU 2014, US 2019 · Melanotan II: none
Afamelanotide is approved only for EPP, as the manufacturer's implant. Melanotan II is approved for no indication anywhere.
Ope…

assertions.text: Afamelanotide is a synthetic analogue of α-MSH.
assertions.quote: Afamelanotide, the first and most studied synthetic α‐MSH analogue, is a nonselective melanocortin tridecapeptide that can bind and activate MC1R.
assertions.note: Böhm 2025 states that afamelanotide is a synthetic analogue of α-MSH.

assertions.text: Melanotan II is a synthetic analogue of α-MSH.
assertions.quote: Melanotan II is a synthetic cyclic α‐MSH analogue that is a nonselective MCR agonist and is not approved for use in any therapeutic indication.

assertions.text: Afamelanotide is a melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R) agonist.
assertions.quote: SCENESSE is a melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1-R) agonist indicated to increase pain free light exposure in adult patients with a history of phototoxic reactions from erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP).

assertions.note: Böhm 2025 notes that Melanotan II crosses the blood-brain barrier, is nonselective, and activates other melanocortin receptors.

assertions.text: Afamelanotide was evaluated in two phase 3 trials in erythropoietic protoporphyria.

units.text:
The evidence
Sixty-nine hours against forty-one.
Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is a rare disorder in which sunlight causes acute, severe pain. In the US phase 3 trial, adults on afamelanotide spent a median 69.4 hours in direct sunlight without pain over six months, against 40.8 hours on placebo. The European trial also showed more pain-free time and fewer phototoxic reactions. Both trials were funded by the manufacturer.
69 vs 41 h
median pain-free hours in direct sunlight over six months, afamelanotide vs placebo (US phase 3 trial, 94 adults with EPP)
Langendonk et al., NEJM 2015 · European trial, 74 adults: 6.0 vs 0.8 hours over nine months
What it means: Afamelanotide lets people with EPP spend more time in sunlight without pain. That is approval-grade evidence (A) for one rare disease.
What it does not mean: It says nothing about cosmetic tanning, about Melanotan II, or about …
