assertions.text: Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is a rare disorder in which sunlight causes acute, severe pain.
assertions.quote: Erythropoietic protoporphyria is a rare, autosomal recessive inborn error of metabolism that typically manifests in early childhood as severe painful photosensitivity.
assertions.note: Langendonk et al. describe EPP as a rare disorder characterized by severe painful photosensitivity.

assertions.text: In the US phase 3 trial involving 94 adults with EPP, patients on afamelanotide spent a median 69.4 hours in direct sunlight without pain over six months compared to 40.8 hours on placebo.
assertions.quote: In the U.S. study, the duration of pain-free time after 6 months was longer in the afamelanotide group (median, 69.4 hours, vs. 40.8 hours in the placebo group; P = 0.04).
assertions.note: The US phase 3 study results report a median 69.4 pain-free hours on afamelanotide versus 40.8 hours on placebo over six months.

assertions.text: In the European trial of 74 adults, afamelanotide resulted in more pain-free sunlight exposure (median 6.0 vs 0.8 hours over nine months) and fewer phototoxic reactions than placebo.
assertions.quote: In the European Union study, the duration of pain-free time after 9 months was also longer in the afamelanotide group than in the placebo group (median, 6.0 hours vs. 0.8 hours; P = 0.005), and the number of phototoxic reactions was lower in the the afamelanotide group (77 vs. 146, P = 0.04).
assertions.note: The European trial confirmed significantly longer pain-free time (6.0 vs 0.8 hours) and fewer phototoxic reactions (77 vs 146).

assertions.text: Both the US and European trials were funded by the manufacturer.
assertions.quote: The study was designed and sponsored by Clinuvel Pharmaceuticals, with input from investigators in the European Union and the United States.
assertions.note: The study design and sponsorship were provided by Clinuvel Pharmaceuticals, the manufacturer.

assertions.text: Afamelanotide allows patients with EPP to spend more time in sunlight without pain.
assertions.quote: Afamelanotide had an acceptable side-effect and adverse-event profile and was associated with an increased duration of sun exposure without pain and improved quality of life in patients with erythropoietic protoporphyria.
assertions.note: The clinical trial conclusion confirms that afamelanotide was associated with an increased duration of sun exposure without pain.

assertions.text: The US label for afamelanotide recommends a full-body skin examination twice a year.
assertions.quote: A full body skin examination (twice yearly) is recommended to monitor pre-existing nevi and new skin pigmentary lesions.
assertions.note: Section 5.2 of the FDA prescribing information recommends a twice-yearly full-body skin examination.

units.text:
Safety signals
What the case reports show.
The harms of Melanotan II come from case reports and reviews, so they show what can happen without telling you how often. Reported skin effects include darkening and growth of existing moles, crops of new and sometimes atypical naevi, and dark bands in the nails. At least five melanomas have been reported during or after use, each in someone with other risk factors, so causation is unproven. Systemic reports include ischaemic priapism needing surgery and a stimulant-like toxic reaction with rhabdomyolysis, and FDA lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious events.
Skin: changing moles, eruptive naevi, melanonychia
Melanoma: reported, causation unproven
Systemic: priapism, rhabdomyolysis, encephalopathy
Narration: Now the harms, and the kind of evidence behind them. Everything here comes from case reports and revie…
units.sourceNote: Habbema 2017 · Cardones 2009 · Paurobally 2013 · Hjuler 2014 · Mallory 2021 · Nelson 2012 · FDA compounding safety page

assertions.text: Reported skin effects of Melanotan II include darkening and growth of existing moles, as well as crops of new and sometimes atypical naevi.
assertions.quote: He developed crops of new pigmented nevi, many of which had atypical clinical and histopathologic features. The preexisting nevi became darker and acquired growth features.
assertions.note: Cardones 2009 describes darkening and growth of preexisting nevi alongside eruptive crops of clinically and histopathologically atypical nevi.

assertions.text: Reported skin effects of Melanotan II include dark bands in the nails (melanonychia).
assertions.quote: Dermatologically it is the opposite of benign: by driving melanogenesis indiscriminately it darkens and enlarges existing moles, provokes eruptive and atypical (dysplastic) nevi and melanonychia, and has been linked in case reports to melanoma arising in pre-existing lesions — causation is unproven, but the mechanism (proliferation of melanocytes, including neoplastic clones) makes it a real concern, and a personal or family history of melanoma is an absolute contraindication.
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni reports that Melanotan II provokes melanonychia among other dermatologic complications.

recheck.note: Hannah-Shmouni reports that Melanotan II provokes melanonychia among other dermatologic complications.

assertions.text: At least five melanomas have been reported during or after Melanotan II use, each in an individual with other risk factors, leaving causation unproven.
assertions.quote: There have been at least five reports of melanomas during or after melanotan II use. All individuals had other risk factors such as fair skin, excess sun exposure/tanning bed use and/or family history of melanoma.
assertions.note: Böhm 2025 notes at least five reported melanomas during or after Melanotan II use, all in individuals who had other melanoma risk factors.

assertions.text: Systemic reports following Melanotan II use include ischaemic priapism requiring surgical decompression.
assertions.quote: This case report highlights a rare presentation of acute ischemic priapism after melanotan II use, managed with surgical decompression.
assertions.note: Mallory 2021 reports acute ischaemic priapism after Melanotan II injection requiring surgical management with penoscrotal decompression.

assertions.text: Systemic reports following Melanotan II use include a stimulant-like toxic reaction with rhabdomyolysis and renal dysfunction.
assertions.quote: This unique case highlights the potential of systemic toxicity with sympathomimetic excess, rhabdomyolysis, and renal dysfunction from Melanotan II use.
assertions.note: Nelson 2012 reports systemic toxicity with sympathomimetic excess, rhabdomyolysis, and renal dysfunction following Melanotan II injection.

assertions.text: The FDA lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious adverse events associated with Melanotan II.
assertions.quote: Published case reports discuss serious adverse events including melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, sympathomimetic toxidrome and priapism.
assertions.note: The FDA safety review page lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among serious adverse events reported in the literature for Melanotan II.

assertions.text: The finding that afamelanotide increases pain-free time in sunlight in erythropoietic protoporphyria is supported by randomized controlled trials in humans.
assertions.quote: We conducted two multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of subcutaneous implants containing 16 mg of afamelanotide.
assertions.note: Two multicenter randomized placebo-controlled trials evaluated afamelanotide in EPP.

assertions.text: In the US phase 3 trial, afamelanotide resulted in a median of 69.4 pain-free hours in direct sunlight over six months compared with 40.8 hours with placebo.

assertions.text: In two phase 3 trials involving 1,200 adults, up to 39% of patients on baricitinib achieved at least 80% scalp hair coverage at 36 weeks compared with 3% to 6% on placebo.
assertions.quote: The estimated percentage of patients with a SALT score of 20 or less at week 36 was 38.8% with 4-mg baricitinib, 22.8% with 2-mg baricitinib, and 6.2% with placebo in BRAVE-AA1 and 35.9%, 19.4%, and 3.3%, respectively, in BRAVE-AA2.
assertions.note: Across 1,200 total patients, SALT 20 or less was achieved by up to 38.8% on 4-mg baricitinib versus 3.3% to 6.2% on placebo at week 36.

assertions.text: Evidence for tanning from Melanotan II is limited to small studies, including a three-volunteer pilot and a ten-man erectile-dysfunction study from the 1990s, with no trials of tanning.

Fictional case
New moles after a summer of tanning shots.
A 27-year-old attends for a skin-quality consultation and mentions injecting a 'tanning peptide' bought online for three months. She has noticed darker moles, several new small ones and a dark stripe along one fingernail. Her mother had melanoma. This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence, and one move clearly comes before the others.
Almost certainly Melanotan II: approved nowhere, unknown strength and purity
New and changing naevi and nail pigmentation are the documented harms
Family history of melanoma: the guide's absolute contraindication

units.text:
Lesson 5.3 · Concept
A Wnt switch and a zinc question.
PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating peptide to a short decoy sequence that stops the protein CXXC5 from binding Dishevelled. Freed from that brake, Wnt/β-catenin signalling rises, and in mice hair regrew faster. Its developers also found CXXC5 raised in human balding scalp. Zinc thymulin is a thymic peptide that is active only when bound to zinc. How it might act on hair has never been defined, and whether any effect would come from the peptide or the zinc is unknown.
PTD-DBM: releases a Wnt brake (mouse data)
Zinc thymulin: a zinc-dependent thymic peptide
Both: mechanism first, human data absent
Narration: Two peptides are sold for hair, and both arrive with better stories than data. PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating fragment borrowed from an HIV protein to a short decoy sequence. Inside follicle cells, the decoy keeps a protein called …

The evidence
Zero trials in people.
As of September 2026, PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov list no human trial of PTD-DBM, published or registered. Its evidence is one 2017 study in mice and human scalp tissue from the developer's group, whose senior author is affiliated with a biotech company. A 2025 review's summary speaks of 'clinical efficacy', yet the review's own text describes PTD-DBM results in mouse models only.

units.text:
The thymulin spray conversation
Fictional case: a woman with a slowly widening central parting has been using a zinc thymulin scalp spray, and asks whether it will work.
What do you tell her first?
Correct answer: Name the grade plainly: D. No indexed human study has tested zinc thymulin for hair.
Explanation: The useful conversation names the grade first. Zinc thymulin's proposed hair effect has no defined mechanism and no indexed human study.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Reassure her: thymulin is a natural thymic hormone, so it should help.
Explanation: Being a thymic hormone says nothing about hair. How it might act on hair has never been defined, and whether any effect would come from the peptide or the zinc is unknown.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Suggest a PTD-DBM spray instead, since it releases a brake on Wnt signalling.

A patient with pattern thinning asks whether a compounded PTD-DBM spray is 'the new minoxidil'. What does the evidence support?
Explanation: A pathway is a hypothesis; the grade tells you how far it has been tested.

Explanation: That is a mechanism argument. There is no human trial of PTD-DBM, so 'works like minoxidil' has nothing behind it.
Correct answer: PTD-DBM has mouse data and no human trial (D); minoxidil has randomized-trial support and US approval (A). Start with the workup and the approved options.

units.text:
Lesson 6.1 · Mechanism
Two hormones, two layers of skin.
Growth hormone acts mostly in the dermis. Its receptor is expressed more by fibroblasts than by keratinocytes, and it increases fibroblast numbers and supports collagen synthesis. IGF-1, made locally by fibroblasts and melanocytes, reaches keratinocytes through the IGF-1 receptor and makes them divide. Human hair follicles even run their own small growth-hormone loop in the laboratory. With age, GH secretion and IGF-1 fall steadily; this is the somatopause.
GH: dermal fibroblasts and collagen
IGF-1: keratinocyte proliferation, supplied locally
Somatopause: GH and IGF-1 fall with age

units.text:
Human evidence
A much-cited skin result, read again.
In 1990 a much-cited New England Journal of Medicine study gave growth hormone for six months to 12 healthy men over 60, with nine untreated men for comparison and no placebo. Lean mass rose and fat fell. Skin thickness rose 7.1%, with P = 0.07, short of statistical significance. A small 1996 randomized trial in 28 older men found 15% more collagen laid down in implanted wound tubes on GH, a laboratory surrogate for repair.

P = 0.07 · nine untreated men as comparison · no placebo
What it means: A skin result still quoted for growth hormone comes from 12 treated men, without a placebo, and it missed statistical significance. Graded on its design, it is D.
What it does not mean: It does not show that GH thins skin or that it fails in true deficiency, and it…

assertions.text: In a 1990 study, growth hormone was administered for six months to 12 healthy men over 60, compared with nine untreated men and no placebo.
assertions.quote: During the treatment period, 12 men (group 1) received approximately 0.03 mg of biosynthetic human growth hormone per kilogram of body weight subcutaneously three times a week, and 9 men (group 2) received no treatment.
assertions.note: Rudman 1990 reports studying 21 healthy men aged 61 to 81, with 12 receiving human growth hormone and 9 receiving no treatment.

assertions.text: In the 1990 study, lean body mass increased, adipose tissue decreased, and skin thickness increased by 7.1% (P = 0.07).

Skin thickness increased 7.1 percent (P = 0.07).
assertions.note: Rudman 1990 reports that growth hormone administration was accompanied by an increase in lean body mass, a decrease in adipose-tissue mass, and a 7.1% increase in skin thickness with P = 0.07.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Deficiency is a diagnosis. Decline is ageing.
In healthy older adults, randomized trials of growth hormone show small shifts in body composition, about 2 kg less fat and 2 kg more lean mass, with more oedema, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and a trend towards diabetes. Strength and endurance change little. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades its advice against treatment A; graded on the trials themselves the evidence is B, and the conclusion is the same. In the US, as of September 2026, knowingly distributing growth hormone for anti-ageing is a federal offence.
Healthy ageing: small body-composition change, more side-effects
Grade B on the trials (guide: A), same conclusion
US: anti-ageing distribution is a federal offence

assertions.text: In healthy older adults, randomized controlled trials of growth hormone show shifts in body composition of approximately 2 kg less fat mass and 2 kg more lean body mass.
assertions.quote: In participants treated with GH compared with those not treated with GH, overall fat mass decreased (change in fat mass, -2.1 kg [95% CI, -2.8 to -1.35] and overall lean body mass increased (change in lean body mass, 2.1 kg [CI, 1.3 to 2.9]) (P < 0.001), and their weight did not change significantly (change in weight, 0.1 kg [CI, -0.7 to 0.8]; P = 0.87).
assertions.note: A systematic review and meta-analysis of trials in healthy older adults showed a 2.1 kg reduction in fat mass and a 2.1 kg increase in lean body mass.

assertions.text: Growth hormone treatment in healthy older adults is associated with significantly higher rates of oedema, arthralgias, carpal tunnel syndrome, and an increased risk or trend towards diabetes and impaired fasting glucose.
assertions.quote: Persons treated with GH were significantly more likely to experience soft tissue edema, arthralgias, carpal tunnel syndrome, and gynecomastia and were somewhat more likely to experience the onset of diabetes mellitus and impaired fasting glucose.
assertions.note: Liu et al. reported significant increases in soft tissue edema, arthralgias, and carpal tunnel syndrome, as well as a higher incidence of diabetes and impaired fasting glucose.

assertions.text: Growth hormone administration in healthy older adults produces little change in muscle strength or cardiovascular endurance.
assertions.quote: Sex steroid + GH increased muscle strength marginally and VO( 2)max in men, but women had no significant change in strength or cardiovascular endurance.
assertions.note: Blackman et al. found that women had no significant change in strength or endurance, and men showed only a marginal strength increase when growth hormone was combined with testosterone.

assertions.text: The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology clinician's guide assigns a Grade A strength of evidence against prescribing growth hormone for healthy older adults.
assertions.quote: Growth hormone in healthy older adults is not recommended — modest body-composition changes are outweighed by edema, arthralgia, insulin resistance, and carpal tunnel, and it is illegal to prescribe for anti-aging in the US GRADE A.[6]
assertions.note: Chapter 14 of the guide recommends against growth hormone in healthy older adults and assigns that advice GRADE A.

assertions.text: In the United States, distributing human growth hormone as an anti-ageing therapy is unlawful.
assertions.quote: Human growth hormone (GH) is widely used as an antiaging therapy, although its use for this purpose has not been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and its distribution as an antiaging agent is illegal in the United States.
assertions.note: Liu et al. state that distribution of growth hormone as an anti-aging agent is illegal in the United States.

units.text:
Lesson 6.2 · Concept
One axis, four ways in.
Somatropin is growth hormone itself. GHRH analogues (sermorelin, tesamorelin, CJC-1295) stimulate the pituitary's GHRH receptor. Ghrelin-receptor agonists (ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and the oral ibutamoren, MK-677) stimulate GH release through a second pituitary receptor. IGF-1 analogues such as IGF-1 LR3 bypass the pituitary altogether. They are sold as one family, and the next moments take them apart.
Replace: somatropin
Stimulate: GHRH analogues and ghrelin-receptor agonists
Bypass: IGF-1 analogues
Narration: Four routes lead into the same axis, and patients rarely know which one they are on. Somatropin is growth hormone itself, made by recombinant technology. GHRH analogues, sermorelin, tesamorelin and CJC-1295, press on the pituitary's releasing-hormone receptor, so the gland releases its own growth hormone in pulses. Ghrelin-receptor ag…

assertions.text: Somatropin is growth hormone itself, produced using recombinant technology.

assertions.note: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone identical to human growth hormone of pituitary origin.

assertions.text: GHRH analogues, including sermorelin, tesamorelin, and CJC-1295, act on the pituitary GHRH receptor to stimulate pulsatile growth hormone secretion.
assertions.quote: Growth hormone–releasing hormone (GHRH) analogues are synthetic peptides designed to stimulate endogenous GH secretion by activating the pituitary GHRH receptor, thereby increasing GH pulsatility and secondarily IGF-1.
assertions.note: GHRH analogues activate the pituitary GHRH receptor to increase endogenous GH pulsatility.

assertions.text: Ghrelin-receptor agonists, including ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6, and oral ibutamoren (MK-677), stimulate GH release via a second pituitary receptor (GHSR-1a).
assertions.quote: Growth hormone–releasing peptides (GHRPs) are short synthetic peptides that stimulate endogenous GH secretion by activating the ghrelin receptor - the growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a (GHSR-1a), at the level of the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary.
assertions.note: Ghrelin-receptor agonists stimulate endogenous GH release through the growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a.

assertions.text: IGF-1 analogues such as IGF-1 LR3 bypass the pituitary and act directly on the IGF-1 receptor.
assertions.quote: Binds IGF-1R (a receptor tyrosine kinase), driving PI3K/AKT/mTOR and MAPK/ERK signaling — muscle protein synthesis, satellite-cell activation, glucose uptake, nitrogen retention, proliferation, and fat oxidation — independently of growth hormone.
assertions.note: IGF-1 LR3 binds directly to the IGF-1 receptor independently of growth hormone.

units.text:
From pituitary to IGF-1 receptor
Put the entry points in order along the axis, from upstream to downstream.
The pituitary: GHRH analogues and ghrelin-receptor agonists

The IGF-1 receptor: IGF-1 analogues

units.text:
The evidence
Zero skin trials.
A PubMed search in September 2026 found no randomized trial with a skin outcome for tesamorelin, CJC-1295, ipamorelin or IGF-1 LR3. The nearest is a 1997 study of a GHRH(1-29) analogue related to sermorelin, in 19 older adults. Skin thickness measured by caliper rose after 16 weeks, compared with a placebo lead-in rather than a parallel control group.

Closest: a 1997 single-blind study of a GHRH(1-29) analogue, 19 older adults, skin thickness by caliper
What it means: Every skin promise made for these peptides rests on mechanism and anecdote. The nearest data are one small study without a parallel control group (D).
What it does not mean: It does not show these peptides harm skin or do nothing for it. It shows the question has never been properl…

assertions.text: Tesamorelin is supported by approval-grade trials for HIV-associated abdominal fat, having received FDA approval in 2010 based on two phase 3 trials.
assertions.quote: It was first approved in the United States in November 2010 (Egrifta) for the reduction of excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV and lipodystrophy, and newer presentations were later introduced to simplify preparation and administration.
assertions.note: The review confirms FDA approval in 2010 for excess abdominal fat in HIV based on phase 3 trials.

assertions.text: Somatropin is approved for adult growth hormone deficiency, whereas in healthy aging growth hormone trials show more adverse effects than benefit.
assertions.quote: Growth hormone in healthy older adults is not recommended — modest body-composition changes are outweighed by edema, arthralgia, insulin resistance, and carpal tunnel, and it is illegal to prescribe for anti-aging in the US GRADE A.[6]
assertions.note: The guide notes somatropin is indicated for true deficiency and that adverse effects outweigh modest benefits in healthy aging.

assertions.text: Sermorelin was formerly approved in the US for pediatric growth hormone deficiency, while adult use shows hormone elevation without proven clinical benefit.
assertions.quote: GEREF (Sermorelin Acetate) injection, 0.5 mg base/vial and 1.0 mg base/vial, is indicated for the treatment of idiopathic growth hormone deficiency (GHD) in children with growth failure, and GEREF (Sermorelin Acetate) injection, 0.05 mg base/amp, is indicated for evaluating the ability of the somatotroph of the pituitary gland to secrete growth hormone.
assertions.note: FDA notice verifies former approval was for idiopathic GHD in children with growth failure.

assertions.text: CJC-1295 with DAC demonstrated multi-day increases in GH and IGF-1 in two phase 1 trials in healthy adults, but has not demonstrated clinical outcomes.
assertions.quote: After a single injection of CJC-1295, there were dose-dependent increases in mean plasma GH concentrations by 2- to 10-fold for 6 d or more and in mean plasma IGF-I concentrations by 1.5- to 3-fold for 9-11 d.
assertions.note: The phase 1 trial report confirms prolonged, multi-day elevation of GH and IGF-1 after a single dose in healthy subjects.

assertions.text: There are no peer-reviewed published human studies on CJC-1295 without DAC.
assertions.quote: By contrast, “CJC-1295 without DAC” remains essentially uncharacterised in the peer-reviewed human literature. To date, no controlled clinical studies have directly evaluated this compound in humans, and assertions regarding physiologic GH pulsatility or improvements in body composition derive largely from extrapolation from related compounds
assertions.note: The review confirms that no controlled clinical studies have directly evaluated CJC-1295 without DAC in humans.

assertions.text: Ipamorelin stimulates growth hormone release, but its only phase 2 clinical trial in postoperative ileus showed no benefit over placebo.
assertions.quote: There were no significant differences between ipamorelin and placebo in the key and secondary efficacy analyses.
assertions.note: The trial abstract notes no significant differences were found between ipamorelin and placebo in postoperative ileus.

assertions.text: No peer-reviewed published human studies exist for IGF-1 LR3.
assertions.quote: At the opposite end, CJC-1295 without DAC, PEG-MGF, and IGF-1 LR3 (tier D) have no peer-reviewed human studies and are supported only by preclinical extrapolation and grey-literature user narratives.
assertions.note: The review categorizes IGF-1 LR3 as having zero peer-reviewed human studies.

assertions.text: Tesamorelin's GRADE A evidence rating belongs to HIV-associated abdominal fat and does not transfer to other indications.
assertions.quote: Tesamorelin is the instructive exception — a GHRH analog that completed the regulatory path for a defined indication (HIV-associated visceral adiposity) GRADE A, showing what real peptide evidence looks like.[2]
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni assigns Grade A specifically to tesamorelin for HIV-associated visceral adiposity, and Dominikowski notes off-label uses remain unproven.

assertions.text: CJC-1295 with and without its albumin-binding tail (DAC) are two distinct products, and only the variant with DAC has been tested in humans.
assertions.quote: By contrast, “CJC-1295 without DAC” remains essentially uncharacterised in the peer-reviewed human literature. To date, no controlled clinical studies have directly evaluated this compound in humans, and assertions regarding physiologic GH pulsatility or improvements in body composition derive largely from extrapolation from related compounds

units.text:
Molecule, evidence, status
A patient says their clinic offers 'CJC', a peptide that raises growth hormone naturally, for skin and sleep, and asks what you think.
What do you establish first?
Correct answer: Which molecule, exactly: CJC-1295 with or without DAC
Explanation: Three answers come before anything else, and this is the first. CJC-1295 with and without its albumin-binding tail are two different products, and only the version with the tail has been tested in people.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Whether it raises IGF-1
Explanation: A higher IGF-1 is a laboratory result. Benefit to a patient needs a clinical trial. First, which molecule, exactly.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Whether other patients' skin improved on it
Explanation: Every skin promise made for these peptides rests on mechanism and anecdote. First, which molecule, exactly.
It is 'Mod …

assertions.text: CJC-1295 with DAC and CJC-1295 without DAC are distinct entities, and only the version with the albumin-binding DAC tail has been tested in humans.
assertions.quote: Two main variants circulate commercially in the off-label market: CJC-1295 with a drug-affinity complex (DAC) and CJC-1295 without DAC. The DAC modification enables binding to circulating albumin, markedly prolonging exposure and enabling a more sustained pharmacodynamic effect after a single administration.
assertions.note: Dominikowski et al. confirm the two variants and note that only CJC-1295 with DAC has human clinical trial data.

assertions.text: There are no peer-reviewed human studies evaluating Mod GRF 1-29 (CJC-1295 without DAC), and claims for it are extrapolated from sermorelin and the DAC version.
assertions.quote: By contrast, “CJC-1295 without DAC” remains essentially uncharacterised in the peer-reviewed human literature. To date, no controlled clinical studies have directly evaluated this compound in humans, and assertions regarding physiologic GH pulsatility or improvements in body composition derive largely from extrapolation from related compounds (primarily GHRH(1–29), known as sermorelin, as previously described), as well as from non-academic sources, rather than from direct clinical evidence.
assertions.note: Dominikowski et al. confirm that CJC-1295 without DAC lacks human studies and its claims are extrapolated from related compounds.

assertions.text: CJC-1295 with DAC was evaluated in two phase 1 trials in healthy adults showing GH and IGF-1 elevations lasting days, without measuring clinical outcomes.
assertions.quote: The best human evidence comes from randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind ascending-dose trials conducted in healthy adults using CJC-1295 DAC administered subcutaneously. In these studies, a single injection produced dose-dependent increases in mean plasma GH (approximately 2- to 10-fold for ≥6 days) and mean plasma IGF-1 (approximately 1.5- to 3-fold for 9–11 days).
assertions.note: Dominikowski et al. and Teichman et al. describe two ascending-dose phase 1 trials in healthy adults demonstrating prolonged GH and IGF-1 elevation without efficacy endpoints.

assertions.text: Tesamorelin is supported by approval-grade clinical trials for the reduction of visceral fat in patients with HIV.
assertions.quote: Our objective was to perform a pooled analysis of two phase-3 studies of tesamorelin in ART-treated HIV patients with excess abdominal fat.
assertions.note: Falutz et al. report pooled phase 3 trials in HIV patients with visceral adiposity, and FDA labeling confirms the indication.

assertions.text: CJC-1295 is not on the 503A bulks list, and the FDA lists its nomination among Category 2 nominations that were withdrawn, citing serious adverse events.
assertions.quote: Compounded drugs containing CJC-1295 may pose risk for immunogenicity for certain routes of administration and may have complexities with regard to for peptide-related impurities and API characterization. FDA has identified serious adverse events associated with CJC-1295 including increased heart rate and systemic vasodilatory reaction. Available clinical data are limited.
assertions.note: The FDA page lists CJC-1295 among withdrawn Category 2 nominations and cites serious adverse events including tachycardia and vasodilation.

units.text:
Lesson 6.3 · Recognition
What too much growth hormone looks like.
Sustained GH excess changes skin in ways you can see. In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema make the face, hands and feet puffy and thick; the skin turns oily with large pores; sweating increases; skin tags and acanthosis nigricans appear. Drugs on this axis bring their own signs: fluid retention with swelling, joint pain, tingling and carpal tunnel symptoms. The Endocrine Society recommends measuring IGF-1 when typical acral and facial features are present.
Soft tissue: puffy, thickened face, hands and feet
Skin: oily, sweaty, skin tags, acanthosis nigricans
On treatment: swelling, joint pain, tingling
Narration: Excess growth hormone leaves visible marks on skin and soft tissue, and noticing them early matters. In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema thicken the face, hands and feet, so featur…
units.sourceNote: Ben-Shlomo & Melmed 2006 · Endocrine Society guideline 2014 · Acromegaly consensus 2024 · somatropin label

assertions.text: In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema cause puffiness and thickening of the face, hands, and feet.
assertions.quote: Skin puffiness due to dermal glycosaminoglycan accumulation and edema are most prominent in the face, hands and feet.
assertions.note: Supported by the review on cutaneous manifestations of acromegaly.

assertions.text: In acromegaly, the skin becomes oily with enlarged pores, sweating increases, and skin tags and acanthosis nigricans appear.
assertions.quote: Oily skin with large pores, hypertrichosis, and excessive sweating are common features. Pigmented skin tags, acanthosis nigricans, and psoriasis are also encountered.
assertions.note: Supported by the cutaneous findings in the review.

assertions.text: In acromegaly, hands and feet enlarge slowly and the jaw widens.
assertions.quote: Characteristic changes in the face and head, including widening and malocclusion of the jaw and macroglossia, as well as enlarged hands, occur insidiously but are often apparent at initial assessment (HQ).
assertions.note: Supported by the consensus statement description of insidious head and hand changes.

assertions.text: Drugs on the growth hormone axis can cause fluid retention manifest as swelling, joint pain, tingling, and carpal tunnel symptoms, which are usually transient.
assertions.quote: Clinical manifestations of fluid retention (e.g., edema, arthralgia, myalgia, nerve compression syndromes including carpal tunnel syndrome/paresthesia) are usually transient and dose dependent.
assertions.note: Supported by the somatropin prescribing information warning on fluid retention.

assertions.note: Supported by the warnings and precautions section of the Genotropin label.

units.text:
Four registers
Does raising IGF-1 cause cancer?
The honest answer has four parts, and each has its own source. Keep them apart, or a mechanism will be heard as a measured risk.
Mechanism
Plausible
IGF-1 receptor signalling drives cell proliferation and survival, which gives any IGF-1-raising product a theoretical concern
Human observation
Modest associations
In large studies, higher natural IGF-1 goes with slightly higher risks of prostate, breast, colorectal and thyroid cancer; reverse causation is not excluded. In one Ecuadorian cohort, people with GH-receptor deficiency had almost no cancer.
Acromegaly
Slightly raised, inconsistently
Pooled studies show about 1.5 times the expected cancer incidence, with the highest estimates from small single-centre series; a Danish nationwide cohort found no clear rise
GH replacement
Largely reassuring
No clear raised risk in 23,984 GH-treated child…
units.sourceNote: Renehan 2004 · Knuppel 2020 · Dal 2018 · Swerdlow 2017 · Boguszewski 2022 · Guevara-Aguirre 2011

assertions.text: IGF-1 receptor signalling drives cell proliferation and survival, giving IGF-1-raising products a theoretical concern for cancer.
assertions.quote: Insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-I and its main binding protein, IGFBP-3, modulate cell growth and survival, and are thought to be important in tumour development.
assertions.note: Preclinical and clinical summaries confirm that IGF-1 modulates cell growth and survival and raises theoretical concerns regarding oncologic risk.

assertions.text: In large studies, higher natural IGF-1 is associated with slightly higher risks of prostate, breast, colorectal, and thyroid cancer.
assertions.quote: Higher IGF-I concentration was associated with increased risks of thyroid cancer [HR per 5 nmol/L higher concentration 1.18; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.37] in addition to colorectal (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.03-1.13), breast (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.07-1.15), and prostate cancer (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.05-1.12), and reduced risks of ovarian and liver cancer.
assertions.note: UK Biobank prospective analyses showed statistically significant modest positive associations between higher IGF-1 and thyroid, colorectal, breast, and prostate cancer.

assertions.text: Reverse causation is not excluded for the observed associations between natural IGF-1 and cancer risks.
assertions.quote: Mean follow-up was 6.9 years and the possibility that the observed associations may be influenced by reverse causality bias cannot be excluded.
assertions.note: The UK Biobank study explicitly states that reverse causality bias cannot be ruled out.

assertions.text: In one Ecuadorian cohort, people with GH-receptor deficiency had almost no cancer.
assertions.quote: The individuals with GHR deficiency (GHRD) exhibited only one non-lethal malignancy and no cases of diabetes, in contrast to 17% cancer and 5% diabetes prevalence in the controls.
assertions.note: The 22-year Ecuadorian study observed only a single non-lethal malignancy among GHRD individuals compared to 17% in unaffected controls.

assertions.text: Pooled studies show about 1.5 times the expected cancer incidence in acromegaly.
assertions.quote: The meta-analysis yielded an SIR of overall cancer of 1.5 (95% CI, 1.2 to 1.8).
assertions.note: The meta-analysis of 23 acromegaly studies found a standardized incidence ratio for overall cancer of 1.5.

assertions.text: The highest cancer incidence estimates in acromegaly come from small single-centre series.
assertions.quote: In general, cancer SIR was higher in single-center studies and in studies with <10 cancer cases.
assertions.note: The meta-analysis observed that standardized incidence ratios were higher in single-center studies and small series.

assertions.text: A Danish nationwide cohort of acromegaly patients found no clear rise in cancer incidence.
assertions.quote: The cohort study identified 81 cases of cancer after exclusion of cases diagnosed within the first year [SIR 1.1; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.9 to 1.4].
assertions.note: The cohort study identified an SIR of 1.1 (0.9 to 1.4), but the provided abstract text does not specify that the cohort was Danish.

assertions.text: No clear raised cancer risk was found in 23,984 GH-treated children with growth failure and no other disease.
assertions.quote: There was no clear raised risk in patients with growth failure without other major disease.
assertions.note: The 23,984 figure represented the entire SAGhE cohort across all diagnoses, whereas the isolated growth failure subgroup comprised 12,468 patients.

assertions.text: A 2022 consensus found no link between GH replacement and primary tumours or cancer recurrence in survivors.
assertions.quote: Current evidence reviewed from the proceedings from the Workshop does not support an association between GH replacement and primary tumour or cancer recurrence.
assertions.note: The 2022 consensus workshop statement reported no association between GH replacement therapy and primary tumour occurrence or recurrence.

assertions.text: No long-term cancer data exist for secretagogues or IGF-1 LR3 used for ageing or skin.
assertions.quote: Given the absence of regulatory approval, the lack of dose standardization, and the limited availability of long-term safety data, patients should be counseled by medical professionals regarding the uncertain oncologic risks associated with sustained activation of the GH–IGF-1 signaling pathway.
assertions.note: The review establishes that long-term safety data and peer-reviewed human trials are lacking for these unregulated compounds.

Tesamorelin is the best-studied peptide on this axis. In its pivotal trials, 47% of treated patients had IGF-1 more than two standard deviations above the mean at 26 weeks, and 36% more than three. Its label states that the effects of prolonged IGF-1 elevation are unknown. For unapproved secretagogues bought for skin, nobody has published the equivalent figure.

Practice
A clinic page, read line by line.
Separate the physiology from the promise.

units.text:
Physiology or promise?
A fictional clinic page for a growth-hormone peptide. Find the lines the evidence does not support.
Sound line: Growth hormone and IGF-1 fall steadily from early adulthood.
Explanation: Sound. GH pulses and IGF-1 fall from early adulthood: the somatopause, a normal part of ageing.
Flagged line (the learner flags it; the course's claim is only that the evidence does not support it): "If your IGF-1 is below the range for a 30-year-old, your body needs topping up."
Explanation: Reference ranges are age-adjusted, so an IGF-1 that is low for a 25-year-old is often normal for the patient's age. Treat a diagnosis, not a number read against the wrong age band.
Sound line: In laboratory studies, growth hormone acts on dermal fibroblasts and supports collagen synthesis.
Explanation: Sound, as mechanism: in culture growth hormone increases fibroblast numbers and supports coll…

assertions.text: Growth hormone and IGF-1 fall steadily from early adulthood (the somatopause).
assertions.quote: The somatopause is the progressive fall in growth-hormone pulse amplitude and IGF-1, beginning in the third decade and among the steepest of all.[2]
assertions.note: The source confirms that the somatopause is the progressive decline of growth hormone and IGF-1 starting in the third decade of life.

recheck.note: The source confirms that the somatopause is the progressive decline of growth hormone and IGF-1 starting in the third decade of life.

assertions.text: Evidence does not support that an IGF-1 level below the reference range for a 30-year-old indicates a need for supplementation, as reference ranges are age-adjusted.
assertions.quote: Because circulating GH is pulsatile and short-lived, isolated random GH measurements are often uninformative, whereas IGF-1 - while imperfect - typically provides a more interpretable integrated signal of pathway activation over time when measured and interpreted using age-adjusted reference ranges.
assertions.note: The review confirms that IGF-1 must be evaluated using age-adjusted reference ranges rather than fixed young-adult thresholds.

assertions.text: In laboratory studies, growth hormone acts on dermal fibroblasts and supports collagen synthesis.
assertions.quote: GH activity, sometimes mediated via IGF-I, is primarily evident in the dermis, particularly affecting collagen synthesis.
assertions.note: The cited review confirms that growth hormone activity in the dermis particularly affects collagen synthesis.

assertions.text: Evidence does not support that CJC-1295 and ipamorelin injections are clinically proven to thicken skin.
assertions.quote: At the opposite end, CJC-1295 without DAC, PEG-MGF, and IGF-1 LR3 (tier D) have no peer-reviewed human studies and are supported only by preclinical extrapolation and grey-literature user narratives.
assertions.note: The review establishes that CJC-1295 without DAC has no peer-reviewed human trials and lacks controlled clinical outcome data.

assertions.text: Tesamorelin is FDA-approved since 2010 to reduce excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy.
assertions.quote: It was first approved in the United States in November 2010 (Egrifta) for the reduction of excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV and lipodystrophy, and newer presentations were later introduced to simplify preparation and administration.
assertions.note: The text confirms tesamorelin's 2010 FDA approval for HIV-associated lipodystrophy.

assertions.text: Evidence does not support that non-approved peptide blends carry the same clinical backing as tesamorelin.
assertions.quote: With the singular exception of tesamorelin within its approved HIV-lipodystrophy indication, none of these compounds carry regulatory approval for performance- or appearance-related use, and tesamorelin trial data should not be extrapolated to hypertrophy or athletic indications.
assertions.note: The source emphasizes that tesamorelin's trial data and approval do not apply to other peptides or off-label indications.

assertions.text: Evidence does not support that growth-hormone axis peptides are free of side-effects, as they cause fluid retention, arthralgia, and other adverse effects.
assertions.quote: Reported adverse effects span endocrine and metabolic disturbances (including prolactin and cortisol elevations, appetite changes, and dysglycaemia), fluid retention syndromes, musculoskeletal symptoms (myalgia/arthralgia), and injection-site reactions.
assertions.note: The source documents that GH-axis peptides cause fluid retention syndromes, musculoskeletal symptoms, and metabolic disturbances.

Her rings no longer fit, her face and hands look puffy, her fingers tingle at night, she sweats more, and new skin tags have appeared on her neck. She asks for a stronger version. Role version (clinical-staff): You record the product name, supplier and duration, note the swelling and tingling, and escalate to the prescriber the same day.
Role version (advisor): You advise her to stop, keep the vial and packaging, and see a prescribe…

Explanation: That turns a mechanism into a measured risk. The mechanism is plausible; the effect of this product on cancer has never been studied.

units.text:
Lesson 7.1 · Concept
GRADE rates certainty in an effect, one outcome at a time.
GRADE sorts the evidence on a specific question into four levels of certainty: high, moderate, low and very low. The rating applies to a body of evidence for one outcome, never to a single study or to a molecule. Randomized trials start high and observational studies start low; certainty then falls for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or suspected publication bias, and occasionally rises for a very large effect. Both Hormonaly guides print the letters A to D for the same idea, adapted, and attach each letter to a specific use.
Four levels, applied to a body of evidence
Five named reasons to rate down
The letter belongs to a use, never to a molecule
Narration: Every claim you hear about a skin peptide carries a hidden question. How sure can we be? GRADE answers it with four levels of cert…

units.text:
Who paid
Sponsored studies come out better.
A Cochrane methodology review brought together 75 papers, each comparing studies sponsored by the manufacturer with studies funded in other ways. Industry-sponsored drug and device studies more often reported favourable efficacy results and favourable conclusions, and the difference was not explained by the usual risk-of-bias checks. It is the pattern you met with oral collagen in module 04.
1.27
risk ratio for a favourable efficacy result, industry-sponsored versus other studies
Lundh et al., Cochrane 2017 · 95% CI 1.17–1.37 · moderate-certainty evidence
What it means: When a manufacturer pays for the trial, a favourable result is more likely. Funding is a reason to read a trial harder and to look for independent replication.
What it does not mean: It does not make a sponsored trial wrong or an independent one right. It describes an average ti…

assertions.text: A Cochrane methodology review brought together 75 papers comparing studies sponsored by the manufacturer with studies funded in other ways.

assertions.note: The review included 75 papers comparing industry-sponsored studies with studies having other funding sources.

assertions.text: Industry-sponsored drug and device studies more often reported favourable efficacy results and conclusions, with the difference not explained by standard risk-of-bias checks.
assertions.quote: Sponsorship of drug and device studies by the manufacturing company leads to more favorable efficacy results and conclusions than sponsorship by other sources. Our analyses suggest the existence of an industry bias that cannot be explained by standard 'Risk of bias' assessments.
assertions.note: The Cochrane review concluded that industry sponsorship leads to more favourable results and conclusions not explained by standard risk of bias assessments.

assertions.text: The pooled risk ratio for a favourable efficacy result in industry-sponsored versus other studies is 1.27 (95% CI 1.17–1.37), supported by moderate-certainty evidence.

What changes in practice
Two checks, never one.
Evidence grade and regulatory status are separate axes, and both Hormonaly guides ask you to clear both. An approved drug can carry a low grade for the use a patient wants, and a compound with stronger human data can still have no lawful route. A plausible mechanism never raises a grade. Say the outcome, the grade and who ran the trials, then check the status as its own step.
Grade: certainty for this outcome
Status: what the law allows, checked separately
Mechanism never raises a grade

What does each one do to the certainty of the evidence for that outcome?

Explanation: A persuasive mechanism leaves the grade exactly where it is. Both Hormonaly guides say so in almost the same words.

assertions.text: A body of evidence consisting of small, commercially funded studies lowers certainty due to suspected publication bias, which is a reason to rate down.
assertions.quote: For publication bias, a body of evidence comprising small studies funded by industry should raise suspicion.
assertions.note: Core GRADE notes that small studies funded by industry raise suspicion of publication bias to rate down certainty.

assertions.text: A persuasive mechanism leaves the evidence grade where it is, as stated in the Hormonaly guides.
assertions.quote: Mechanistic appeal alone never raises a grade.
assertions.note: The Peptide Pocket Guide explicitly notes that mechanistic appeal alone never raises a grade.

assertions.text: A very large effect can raise certainty in evidence rating.
assertions.quote: Core GRADE users appraising results from well conducted NSRI can consider rating up certainty of evidence when risk ratios from pooled estimates suggest large or very large effects.
assertions.note: Core GRADE explicitly states that large or very large effects are grounds to consider rating up certainty.

assertions.text: A drug's approval for a different use leaves the evidence grade where it is, as regulatory status and evidentiary certainty are separate axes.
assertions.quote: An FDA-approved drug may carry a lower grade for a particular off-label use than an investigational compound supported by stronger human evidence; regulatory status and evidentiary certainty are separate axes.
assertions.note: The source notes that an FDA-approved drug may carry a lower grade for an off-label use and that regulatory status and evidentiary certainty are separate axes.

assertions.text: When a confidence interval spans an important effect and little to no effect due to too few events or people, it lowers certainty for imprecision.
assertions.quote: For instance, using the MID thresholds, a point estimate greater than the MID suggests an important effect and less than the MID, an unimportant or little to no effect. Users then rate down for imprecision if the 95% confidence interval crosses the MID for benefit or harm.
assertions.note: Core GRADE explains that users rate down for imprecision if the 95% confidence interval crosses the minimal important difference (MID) between an important effect and little to no effect.

assertions.text: Being the peptide patients ask for most leaves the grade where it is, as GRADE reflects evidence for a listed use rather than popularity.
assertions.quote: Every entry carries a GRADE letter. GRADE reflects the strength of the clinical evidence for the listed use — not mechanistic plausibility, popularity, compounding availability, or clinical fashion.
assertions.note: The source confirms that GRADE reflects clinical evidence rather than popularity or clinical fashion.

units.text:
A fictional serum's brochure says 'GRADE A: three randomized trials'. All three were run by the maker, enrolled 20 to 30 people each, lasted four weeks and measured skin hydration. Your patient wants fewer wrinkles. What is the most defensible certainty for that outcome?
Explanation: Grade the outcome the patient wants, then name what lowers it.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): High, because three randomized trials agree.
Explanation: Randomized trials start high, but these are small, sponsor-run and measured a different outcome, and each of those lowers certainty.
Correct answer: Low or very low: small sponsor-run trials that measured hydration, not wrinkles.
Explanation: Correct. Indirectness (the wrong outcome), imprecision (few people) and suspected publication bias (small industry-funded studies) all rate it down.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): It cannot …

assertions.text: In the GRADE approach, randomized controlled trials start as high-certainty evidence.
assertions.quote: In Core GRADE, randomised controlled trials begin as high certainty evidence and non-randomised studies of interventions (NRSI) as low certainty.
assertions.note: The abstract explicitly states that randomised controlled trials begin as high certainty evidence in Core GRADE.

assertions.text: Indirectness, such as when study outcomes differ from the target outcome, is a reason to rate down the certainty of evidence.
assertions.quote: When target and study PICOs differ substantially, studies provide indirect evidence and Core GRADE users may rate down the certainty of evidence as a result of this indirectness.
assertions.note: Core GRADE users may rate down certainty when the target and study PICOs differ substantially.

assertions.text: Evidence certainty can be rated down due to imprecision.
assertions.quote: This second article in a seven part series presents the Core GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach to deciding on the target of the certainty rating, and decisions about rating down certainty of evidence due to imprecision.
assertions.note: The Core GRADE series addresses rating down certainty of evidence due to imprecision.

assertions.text: A body of evidence consisting of small industry-funded studies raises suspicion of publication bias in GRADE.
assertions.quote: For publication bias, a body of evidence comprising small studies funded by industry should raise suspicion.
assertions.note: Core GRADE notes that small studies funded by industry should raise suspicion of publication bias.

units.text:
Lesson 7.2 · Concept
Two compounding routes, one strict order.
In the US, section 503A lets a licensed pharmacist or physician compound for an identified patient on a prescription, exempt from new-drug approval, adequate directions for use and good manufacturing practice. The bulk substance must meet a USP or NF monograph; failing that, be a component of an approved drug; failing that, appear on FDA's 503A bulks list. It must also come from an FDA-registered establishment with a valid certificate of analysis. Section 503B outsourcing facilities register with FDA, work to good manufacturing practice under inspection, and may compound without patient-specific prescriptions.
503A: patient-specific, three exemptions
Monograph, then approved component, then the bulks list
503B: registered, inspected, held to good manufacturing practice
Narration: Two routes exist for compounding in the United…
units.sourceNote: 21 U.S.C. 353a and 353b · FDA 503A bulks page (updated 14 May 2026) · FDA, information for outsourcing facilities

assertions.text: Under section 503A, a licensed pharmacist or physician can compound for an identified patient on a prescription, exempt from new-drug approval, adequate directions for use, and good manufacturing practice.
assertions.quote: Sections 351(a)(2)(B) , 352(f)(1) , and 355 of this title shall not apply to a drug product if the drug product is compounded for an identified individual patient based on the receipt of a valid prescription order or a notation, approved by the prescribing practitioner, on the prescription order that a compounded product is necessary for the identified patient
assertions.note: Section 503A exempts compounded drugs prepared by licensed pharmacists or physicians for individual patients from sections 351(a)(2)(B), 352(f)(1), and 355.

assertions.text: For 503A compounding, bulk drug substances must meet a USP or NF monograph; failing that, be a component of an FDA-approved drug; failing that, appear on FDA's 503A bulks list.
assertions.quote: State-licensed physicians and pharmacists that compound under section 503A of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) may only compound drug products using bulk drug substances that: Comply with an applicable United States Pharmacopeia (USP) or National Formulary (NF) monograph if one exists, and the USP chapter on pharmacy compounding; Are components of FDA-approved drug products if an applicable USP or NF monograph does not exist; or Appear on FDA’s list of bulk drug substances that can be used in compounding (the 503A bulks list) if such a monograph does not exist and the substance is not a component of an FDA-approved drug product.
assertions.note: The statute and FDA page mandate this exact three-tier hierarchical standard for bulk drug substances.

assertions.text: Bulk drug substances used under section 503A must come from an FDA-registered establishment and be accompanied by a valid certificate of analysis.
assertions.quote: In addition, bulk drug substances must be accompanied by a valid certificate of analysis and must have been manufactured by an establishment registered with FDA under section 510 of the FD&C Act.
assertions.note: FDA guidance and the statute require registration of the manufacturing establishment and a valid certificate of analysis.

assertions.text: Section 503B outsourcing facilities register with the FDA, must comply with current good manufacturing practice, and are inspected on a risk-based schedule.
assertions.quote: Outsourcing facilities: must comply with CGMP requirements; are inspected by FDA according to a risk-based schedule; and must meet certain other conditions, such as reporting adverse events and providing FDA with certain information about the products they compound.
assertions.note: Outsourcing facilities must comply with CGMP, register, and are subject to risk-based FDA inspections.

assertions.text: Section 503B outsourcing facilities may compound without patient-specific prescriptions, and their compounded products remain unapproved by FDA.
assertions.quote: Drugs compounded by an outsourcing facility can qualify for exemptions from FDA approval requirements and the requirement to label products with adequate directions for use, but not from current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements.
assertions.note: The law explicitly permits compounding without individual patient prescriptions, and products qualify for exemption from FDA approval requirements.

units.text: In the EU, medicines prepared in a pharmacy on prescription for an individual patient (magistral formulas) or to a pharmacopoeia for the pharmacy's own patients (officinal formulas) are outside Directive 2001/83/EC (Article 3). Pharmacists who prepare medicines solely for retail supply in dispensing pharmacies are also exempt from manufacturing authorisation (Article 40(2)).

assertions.text: In the EU, medicinal products prepared in a pharmacy on prescription for an individual patient (magistral formula) or in accordance with a pharmacopoeia for the pharmacy's own patients (officinal formula) are outside Directive 2001/83/EC under Article 3.
assertions.quote: This Directive shall not apply to: 1. Any medicinal product prepared in a pharmacy in accordance with a medical prescription for an individual patient (commonly known as the magistral formula). 2. Any medicinal product which is prepared in a pharmacy in accordance with the prescriptions of a pharmacopoeia and is intended to be supplied directly to the patients served by the pharmacy in question
assertions.note: Directive 2001/83/EC Article 3 explicitly excludes magistral and officinal formulas prepared in a pharmacy.

assertions.text: Under Article 40(2) of Directive 2001/83/EC, manufacturing authorisation is not required for preparation carried out solely for retail supply by pharmacists in dispensing pharmacies.
assertions.quote: However, such authorization shall not be required for preparation, dividing up, changes in packaging or presentation where these processes are carried out, solely for retail supply, by pharmacists in dispensing pharmacies or by persons legally authorized in the Member States to carry out such processes.
assertions.note: Article 40(2) explicitly exempts preparation solely for retail supply by pharmacists in dispensing pharmacies from manufacturing authorisation.

units.text: In Portugal, a magistral formula is prepared in a community or hospital pharmacy on a medical prescription naming the patient, under a pharmacist's responsibility (Decreto-Lei 95/2004). Compounded medicines may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese or European pharmacopoeia, another European pharmacopoeia or compendial scientific documentation, and one containing any other raw material may not be prescribed.

assertions.note: Decreto-Lei 95/2004 defines a magistral formula as prepared in a community or hospital pharmacy under medical prescription for a specified patient under a pharmacist's responsibility.

units.text: In Brazil, a magistral preparation is made individually by a pharmacy against a prescription from an authorised professional (RDC 96/2008). ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that any substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded, and that compounding may take place only individually, on a medical prescription, in a pharmacy licensed by local health surveillance.

units.text: In the UAE, where the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has regulated medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies are exempt from marketing approval under Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024 (Art. 5(2)), although such a pharmacy may not copy an EDE-approved product unless no commercial product can deliver the expected benefit, nor formulate products for research, development or experimentation (Art. 95). In Abu Dhabi, the DoH's compounding standard (August 2026) treats peptides as high-risk substances and lets novel substances of unknown risk be compounded only if monographed, a component of an approved medicine or listed on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances. In Dubai, the DHA prohibits prescribing, dispensing or using any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026).

Practice
The substance, in strict order.
In the US, the conditions for 503A compounding start with the substance itself, taken in strict order.

assertions.text: In the US, the conditions for 503A compounding start with the substance itself, taken in strict order.

assertions.note: Federal law establishes a strict sequential order for qualifying bulk drug substances under section 503A.

assertions.text: The 503A bulks list is addressed through notice-and-comment rulemaking, whereas FDA's categories represent an interim enforcement policy while nominations are evaluated.
assertions.quote: The agency also will continue to evaluate bulk drug substances that have been nominated with sufficient supporting information and address those substances on a rolling basis through notice-and-comment rulemaking.
assertions.note: FDA evaluates bulk drug substance nominations and addresses them through notice-and-comment rulemaking, using categories as an interim policy.

assertions.text: The 503A bulks list in 21 CFR 216.23 contains six substances, none of which is a peptide, and has remained unchanged since the February 2019 final rule.
assertions.quote: A final regulation was issued in February 2019, List of Bulk Drug Substances That Can Be Used To Compound Drug Products in Accordance with Section 503A of the FD&C Act , in which FDA placed six substances on the list, identified and did not place four other substances on the list, and established the criteria to evaluate substances for inclusion on the list.
assertions.note: FDA placed six non-peptide substances on the 503A bulks list in February 2019.

assertions.text: Inclusion of a substance on the 503A bulks list does not carry FDA endorsement or demonstration of safety or efficacy.
assertions.quote: Based on evidence currently available, there are inadequate data to demonstrate the safety or efficacy of any drug product compounded using any of the drug substances listed in paragraph (a) of this section, or to establish general recognition of the safety or effectiveness of any such drug product.
assertions.note: 21 CFR 216.23 specifies there are inadequate data to establish safety or efficacy and prohibits representing listed bulks as FDA approved or endorsed.

assertions.text: FDA does not intend to take action against compounders using Category 1 bulk drug substances provided guidance conditions are met.
assertions.quote: FDA does not intend to take action against a compounder for compounding drugs using bulk drug substances listed in category 1, provided that the conditions described in the guidance document are met.
assertions.note: FDA's interim policy states the agency does not intend to take action regarding Category 1 substances if conditions are satisfied.

assertions.text: GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes of administration is placed in Category 1 as of the May 14, 2026 update.
assertions.quote: GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) will be added back to category 1.
assertions.note: The May 14, 2026 category update added GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes back to Category 1.

assertions.text: Category 2 includes bulk drug substances for which FDA has identified significant safety risks.
assertions.quote: Category 2 – These substances were nominated with sufficient supporting information to permit FDA to evaluate them, and they may be eligible for inclusion on the 503A bulks list. However, FDA has identified significant safety risks relating to the use of these substances in compounding pending further evaluation and, therefore, does not intend to adopt the policy described for the substances in category 1.
assertions.note: Category 2 substances are those nominated with adequate information but identified by FDA as presenting significant safety risks.

assertions.text: Nominations for substances such as BPC-157, TB-500, and KPV were withdrawn by nominators, and FDA maintains summaries of identified safety risks for withdrawn substances.
assertions.quote: This list of bulk drug substances previously in category 2 of the interim policies were withdrawn by the nominators.
assertions.note: FDA publishes a list of bulk drug substances previously in Category 2 whose nominations were withdrawn, retaining their safety risk evaluations.

assertions.text: FDA staff concluded that statutory evaluation criteria weigh against placing BPC-157 on the 503A bulks list, while advisory committee recommendations serve as advice only.

assertions.note: FDA staff determined that evaluation criteria weigh against placing BPC-157 on the 503A bulks list.

units.text:
Peptide or biologic
Forty amino acids.
Since 23 March 2020 FDA defines a protein as an alpha amino acid polymer of more than 40 amino acids, whether or not it is chemically synthesized, so anything above the line is a biological product. On that date tesamorelin, a 44-residue GHRH analogue, and the enzyme hyaluronidase moved to biologics licences, and FDA told compounders that transitioned biologics cannot use the 503A or 503B exemptions.
amino acids: above this, FDA treats the molecule as a protein, and so as a biological product
85 FR 10057, effective 23 March 2020 · tesamorelin (44 residues) and hyaluronidase moved to biologics licences
What it means: Size decides the rulebook. Peptides of 40 or fewer alpha amino acids stay drugs, so the 503A questions apply; above 40 the product is a biologic, and the compounding exemptions are closed to it.
What it does not mean: It does not make a …
units.sourceNote: 85 FR 10057 (2020) · FDA notice to compounders, March 2020 · FDA deemed-BLA list · Eli Lilly v. Kennedy (S.D. Ind. 2025; 7th Cir. No. 26-1301)

assertions.text: Since 23 March 2020, FDA defines a protein as an alpha amino acid polymer of more than 40 amino acids, whether or not chemically synthesized, classifying products above this size as biological products.
assertions.quote: Under the final rule, the term protein means any alpha amino acid polymer with a specific defined sequence that is greater than 40 amino acids in size.
assertions.note: FDA's final rule defines a protein as an alpha amino acid polymer of greater than 40 amino acids in size.

assertions.text: Tesamorelin is a 44-residue growth hormone-releasing factor analogue.
assertions.quote: Tesamorelin is a human growth hormone-releasing factor (GRF) analog produced synthetically. It is comprised of the 44 amino acid sequence of human GRF and a hexenoyl moiety, a C6 chain with a double bond at position 3, attached to the tyrosine residue at the N-terminal part of the molecule.
assertions.note: The prescribing information confirms tesamorelin is a synthetic human GRF analog comprised of 44 amino acids.

assertions.text: FDA informed compounders that biological products transitioning to biologics licenses cannot use the 503A or 503B exemptions.
assertions.quote: This transition affects compounding under sections 503A and 503B of the FD&C Act because, beginning on March 23, these transitioning biological products will not be eligible for the exemptions for compounded drugs under sections 503A and 503B of the FD&C Act.
assertions.note: FDA's notice explicitly states transitioning biologics are ineligible for compounding exemptions under sections 503A and 503B.

units.text:
Regulatory status (outside the US)
Outside the US, 503A does not apply.
FDA's 503A bulks list and its categories are US law and policy and apply only in the US. In the other jurisdictions in this course, a medicine without a marketing authorisation reaches a patient as a pharmacy preparation or an unlicensed supply made on a prescription, and the prescriber answers for that choice.
FDA's bulks list and categories
US only
Set under US federal law and FDA policy; no other jurisdiction in this course applies them.
The route
A pharmacy preparation or an unlicensed supply
Made or supplied on a prescription, for a product with no marketing authorisation in that jurisdiction.
Responsibility
The prescriber's
The prescriber answers for choosing a medicine without a marketing authorisation.
Callout: A 503A category means nothing outside the US: name the route your own law provides, and check it on…

assertions.text: Section 503A and FDA's 503A bulks list and categories are established under US federal law and FDA policy, applying in the US.
assertions.quote: “Section 503A of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act [ 21 U.S.C. 353a ], added by subsection (a), shall take effect upon the expiration of the 1-year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act [ Nov. 21, 1997 ].”
assertions.note: Section 503A is an enactment of the US Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

assertions.text: In the other jurisdictions in the course, a medicine without a marketing authorisation reaches a patient as a pharmacy preparation or an unlicensed supply made on a prescription.
assertions.quote: A Member State may, in accordance with legislation in force and to fulfil special needs, exclude from the provisions of this Directive medicinal products supplied in response to a bona fide unsolicited order, formulated in accordance with the specifications of an authorised health-care professional and for use by an individual patient under his direct personal responsibility.

assertions.text: The prescriber bears responsibility and answers for choosing a medicine without a marketing authorisation.
assertions.quote: The responsibility that falls on healthcare professionals when prescribing an unlicensed medicine or a medicine off-label may be greater than when prescribing a licensed medicine within the terms of its licence.
assertions.note: Prescribers bear responsibility when choosing and prescribing an unlicensed medicinal product.

units.text: The UK handles unlicensed medicines by a different route. A medicine with no UK marketing authorisation may be supplied to meet one patient's special needs, made to a prescriber's specification by a manufacturer that holds a specials licence, and it may not be advertised. The route (regulation 167): One patient, one prescriber, an unsolicited order. Made to the specification of a doctor, dentist, nurse or pharmacist independent prescriber or supplementary prescriber, for a patient under their direct care. No advertisement may be published. Who makes it: A manufacturer with a specials licence. The site is inspected for good manufacturing practice; the product itself is otherwise unassessed for safety, quality and efficacy. A pharmacist may also prepare a medicine in a registered pharmacy against a prescription. Special need: The patient's clinical need. MHRA's examples include an intolera…

assertions.text: A medicine with no UK marketing authorisation may be supplied under regulation 167 of the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 to meet one patient's special needs, made to a prescriber's specification by a manufacturer that holds a specials licence, in response to an unsolicited order, and it may not be advertised.
assertions.quote: 167. —(1) The prohibitions in regulation 46 (requirement for authorisation) do not apply in relation to a medicinal product (a “special medicinal product”) if— (a) the medicinal product is supplied in response to an unsolicited order; (b) the medicinal product is manufactured and assembled in accordance with the specification of a person who is a doctor, dentist, nurse independent prescriber, pharmacist independent prescriber or supplementary prescriber;
assertions.note: Regulation 167 of the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 provides an exemption for special medicinal products manufactured to a prescriber's specification in response to an unsolicited order, provided no advertisement is published.

assertions.text: Under regulation 167, the medicine must be made to the specification of a doctor, dentist, nurse independent prescriber, pharmacist independent prescriber or supplementary prescriber, for a patient under their direct care.
assertions.quote: (b) the medicinal product is manufactured and assembled in accordance with the specification of a person who is a doctor, dentist, nurse independent prescriber, pharmacist independent prescriber or supplementary prescriber; (c) the medicinal product is for use by a patient for whose treatment that person is directly responsible in order to fulfil the special needs of that patient
assertions.note: Regulation 167 explicitly lists these prescriber categories and specifies that the medicine must be for a patient for whose treatment that person is directly responsible.

assertions.text: Under regulation 167, no advertisement relating to the special medicinal product may be published.
assertions.quote: (3) Condition B is that no advertisement relating to the medicinal product is published by any person.
assertions.note: Condition B in regulation 167 prohibits the publication of any advertisement relating to the product.

assertions.text: A UK special manufacturer's site is inspected for good manufacturing practice, but the product itself is otherwise unassessed for safety, quality and efficacy.
assertions.quote: If none of these options will suffice, then a completely unlicensed product may have to be used, for example, UK manufactured "specials", which are made in GMP inspected facilities, but which are otherwise un-assessed (GMP inspection of “specials” manufacturers is not product specific).
assertions.note: MHRA guidance confirms the manufacturing site is inspected for GMP, but the unlicensed product itself is otherwise unassessed for quality, safety, and efficacy.

assertions.text: A pharmacist may also prepare an unlicensed medicine in a registered pharmacy against a prescription.
assertions.quote: (1) ... The restrictions imposed by regulations 17(1) (manufacturing of medicinal products) and 46 (requirement for authorisation) of the 2012 Regulations do not apply to anything which is done in a registered pharmacy, a hospital , a care home service or a health centre and is done there by or under the supervision of a pharmacist and consists of— (a) preparing or dispensing a medicinal product in accordance with a prescription given by an appropriate practitioner
assertions.note: Section 10 of the Medicines Act 1968 provides an exemption for pharmacists preparing or dispensing medicinal products in a registered pharmacy in accordance with a prescription.

assertions.text: MHRA's examples of special clinical need include an intolerance or allergy to an ingredient, or an inability to swallow solid oral dosage forms.
assertions.quote: Examples of “special needs” include an intolerance or allergy to a particular ingredient, or an inability to ingest solid oral dosage forms. These examples are not exhaustive.
assertions.note: MHRA Guidance Note 14 specifically lists an intolerance or allergy to an ingredient, or an inability to ingest solid oral dosage forms, as examples of special needs.

assertions.text: Reasons of cost, convenience, and operational needs do not count as special needs under MHRA guidance.
assertions.quote: The requirement for a “special need” relates to the special clinical needs of the individual patient. It does not include reasons of cost, convenience or operational needs (see Section 10 of this guide).
assertions.note: MHRA Guidance Note 14 states that special clinical needs do not include reasons of cost, convenience, or operational needs.

assertions.text: MHRA's hierarchy of preference for meeting a special need is: UK licensed medicine (even off-label), then an imported medicine licensed in its country of origin, then a UK special, and least acceptable are products not classed as medicines where made, such as supplements.
assertions.quote: 2. Although MHRA does not recommend "off label" (outside of the licensed indications) use of products, if the UK licensed product can meet the clinical need, even "off-label", it should be used instead of an unlicensed product. [...] 3. If the UK product cannot meet the special need, then another (imported) medicinal product should be considered, which is licensed in the country of origin. 4. If none of these options will suffice, then a completely unlicensed product may have to be used, for example, UK manufactured "specials" [...] 5. The least acceptable products are those that are unlicensed in the country of origin, and which are not classed as medicines in the country of origin
assertions.note: Appendix 2 of MHRA Guidance Note 14 details this exact five-tiered hierarchy of preference.

assertions.text: When prescribing an unlicensed medicine, the prescriber must be satisfied the evidence supports safety and efficacy, take responsibility for the prescription and follow-up, record reasons, and explain them to the patient when use is not routine or innovative.
assertions.quote: be satisfied that there is a sufficient evidence base and/or experience of using the medicine to show its safety and efficacy; take responsibility for prescribing the medicine and for overseeing the patient’s care, including monitoring and follow-up; record the medicine prescribed and, where common practice is not being followed, the reasons for prescribing this medicine; [...] you explain the reasons for prescribing a medicine off-label or prescribing an unlicensed medicine where there is little evidence to support its use, or where the use of a medicine is innovative
