Closing Module 7: which statement keeps evidence, regulatory status and product quality apart?
Explanation: Grade, status and quality: three checks, never one sentence.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The certificate shows 99% purity, so the peptide is evidence-based and fine to compound.
Explanation: That blends product quality into evidence and legality. Purity says nothing about whether it works or whether any route is lawful.
Correct answer: Topical GHK-Cu: small-trial evidence (C); in the US, non-injectable use sits in 503A Category 1, under evaluation; its certificate can show identity and purity, never sterility or legality.
Explanation: Correct. Three separate answers, each with its own source.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): GHK-Cu is in Category 1, so it is approved for skin and the evidence question is settled.
Explanation: Category 1 is an enforcem…

assertions.text: Topical GHK-Cu is supported by small-trial evidence and assigned GRADE C.
assertions.quote: Clinical caveat. Evidence base: topical cosmetic RCTs (cosmeceutical use) and preclinical wound-healing models — injectable human use rests on anecdote, no RCTs.
assertions.note: The guide assigns GHK-Cu GRADE C based on topical cosmetic trials.

assertions.text: In the United States, non-injectable GHK-Cu sits in 503A Category 1, under evaluation.
assertions.quote: GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration) will be added back to category 1.
assertions.note: FDA documents list non-injectable GHK-Cu in 503A Category 1 under evaluation.

assertions.text: A certificate of analysis can show identity and purity, but never sterility or legality.
assertions.quote: Compounding pharmacies should provide a COA documenting identity, purity, sterility, and endotoxin.
assertions.note: The guide states that a certificate of analysis can document sterility as well as identity and purity.

assertions.text: 503A Category 1 is an interim enforcement posture while FDA evaluates bulk drug substances, not an approval or evidence determination.
assertions.quote: Categories 1, 2 and 3 are something else: enforcement-discretion postures described in FDA guidance while nominations are evaluated.
assertions.note: The guide confirms Category 1 reflects an enforcement-discretion posture while evaluation is pending rather than statutory approval.

units.text:
A single-cell RNA atlas predicts that a skin cell type can make a hormone. What would move that finding toward proof of secretion?
Explanation: Transcriptomic maps predict capacity; secretion and function need protein-level and functional evidence, and clinical use needs human trials.
Correct answer: Showing the hormone protein and its release by those cells, then its effect in tissue or in people.
Explanation: Correct. RNA is the first rung; protein, release and function are the next.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Finding the same RNA in a second atlas.
Explanation: Replicating the RNA confirms the transcript, which is still a prediction about secretion.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Finding the hormone's receptor RNA in neighbouring cells.
Explanation: That predicts a possible receiver; it does not show the hormone is made or released.

assertions.text: Single-cell transcriptomic predictions of hormone production are hypothesis-generating and require protein-level and functional validation to demonstrate secretion.
assertions.quote: Important: these predictions are based on transcriptomic data and should be considered as putative and hypothesis-generating, rather than as functional hormones and receptors. The user takes responsibility for validation using appropriate methods (e.g. in vitro, in vivo) and for describing appropriately their use of transcriptome-based scores and predictions.
assertions.note: The Hormone Cell Atlas portal notes that transcriptomic predictions must be treated as putative and require experimental validation.

assertions.text: Transcript levels alone are not sufficient to predict cellular protein levels.
assertions.quote: We conclude that transcript levels by themselves are not sufficient to predict protein levels in many scenarios and to thus explain genotype-phenotype relationships and that high-quality data quantifying different levels of gene expression are indispensable for the complete understanding of biological processes.
assertions.note: Liu et al. explicitly conclude that transcript levels alone cannot reliably predict protein levels.

assertions.text: Clinical use requires human trials.
assertions.note: The provided sources focus on basic cell atlasing and mRNA-protein correlation, and do not discuss clinical trials.

units.text:
Which finding is a local cutaneous feedback loop rather than systemic endocrine signalling?
Explanation: A local loop is made and used within the skin; systemic signals travel through the blood, in either direction.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Skin-made vitamin D3 carried by the blood to the liver.
Explanation: That is the skin supplying a whole-body hormone system: skin to body.
Correct answer: Human scalp follicles in culture secrete cortisol and then reduce their own CRH.
Explanation: Correct. Made, sensed and fed back within the follicle, with no systemic connection.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Thin skin and striae in Cushing syndrome.
Explanation: Circulating cortisol excess acting on the skin: body to skin.

assertions.text: Human scalp hair follicles in culture synthesize and secrete cortisol.
assertions.quote: Isolated human hair follicles secrete substantial levels of cortisol into the culture medium, and this activity is further up-regulated by CRH.
assertions.note: Cultured human hair follicles secrete cortisol into culture medium.

assertions.text: Glucocorticoids down-regulate CRH expression in human hair follicles, establishing a local regulatory feedback loop.
assertions.quote: Finally, human hair follicles display HPA axis-like regulatory feedback systems, since the glucocorticoid receptor agonist hydrocortisone down-regulates follicular CRH expression.
assertions.note: Hydrocortisone down-regulates follicular CRH expression in cultured hair follicles.

units.text:
Why can a blood or saliva cortisol level not tell you how much cortisol a patient's skin is generating?
Explanation: Local tissue cortisol and systemic cortisol are separate: the first is a research mechanism, the second is what diagnostic tests measure.
Correct answer: Because 11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol inside skin cells, and local availability is regulated independently of circulating levels.
Explanation: Correct: a mechanism shown in human skin samples and mice.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because skin cells cannot make or activate cortisol.
Explanation: They can: skin expresses an HPA-like axis, and 11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol locally.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Because saliva and blood cortisol tests are unreliable for everything.
Explanation: Late-night salivary cortisol is a first-line test for Cushing's syndrome; it measures systemic cort…

assertions.text: 11β-HSD1 regenerates cortisol inside skin cells, and local glucocorticoid availability is regulated independently of circulating levels.
assertions.quote: Within target tissues, GC availability is regulated at a prereceptor level, independently of systemic levels, by isozymes of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (11β-HSD) that interconvert active cortisol and inactive cortisone.
assertions.note: Supported by the abstract stating that local glucocorticoid availability is regulated independently of systemic levels by 11β-HSD isozymes in target skin cells.

assertions.text: 11β-HSD1 expression and activity in skin cells has been demonstrated in human skin samples and mice.
assertions.quote: 11β-HSD1 (which activates cortisol), but not 11β-HSD2 (which inactivates cortisol), was expressed in epidermal keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts in human skin and also in outer hair follicle root sheath cells in murine skin.
assertions.note: Supported by findings of 11β-HSD1 expression and ex vivo activity in both human skin cells and murine hair follicle cells.

assertions.text: Skin expresses an HPA-like axis.
assertions.note: The provided abstract does not mention a cutaneous or skin HPA-like axis.

assertions.text: Late-night salivary cortisol is a first-line diagnostic test for Cushing's syndrome.
assertions.quote: We recommend initial use of one test with high diagnostic accuracy (urine cortisol, late night salivary cortisol, 1 mg overnight or 2 mg 48-h dexamethasone suppression test).
assertions.note: Supported by the guideline recommendation for initial diagnostic testing.

units.text:
A patient asks whether starting hormone therapy at menopause will stop her wrinkles. Which answer fits the evidence?
Explanation: Separate structural effects (small trials) from visible ageing (large trials) and from indications (symptoms and bone).
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Yes: estrogen rebuilds collagen, so her wrinkles will improve.
Explanation: Small trials show thicker skin, but the largest trials found no difference in wrinkles.
Correct answer: It may thicken the skin a little, the largest trials found no difference in wrinkles, and skin is not a reason to start; hot flashes or vaginal symptoms are worth discussing with a prescriber.
Explanation: Correct: a secondary effect, and an indication-led decision.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): It has no effect on skin at all.
Explanation: Small RCTs do show gains in thickness and collagen; what is unpro…

assertions.text: Small trials show that hormone therapy can thicken the skin.
assertions.quote: Treatment with conjugated estrogens for 12 months significantly increases, at the level of the right great trochanter, the thickness of the skin (p < 0.01), as assessed by ultrasonography, and of the dermis (p < 0.05), as assessed by skin biopsy.
assertions.note: A small randomized controlled trial demonstrated that conjugated estrogens significantly increased skin and dermal thickness.

assertions.text: The largest clinical trials of hormone therapy found no statistically significant difference in wrinkles compared to placebo.
assertions.quote: There were slight decreases in all parameters for all treatment groups for the primary subject end points, but there were no statistically significant differences between the NA/EE groups and placebo.
assertions.note: A large RCT evaluating hormone therapy found no significant differences in facial wrinkling compared to placebo.

assertions.text: Skin aging is not an approved indication to initiate hormone therapy, whereas hot flashes and vaginal symptoms are recognized indications.
assertions.quote: The FDA has approved multiple hormone therapies for moderate-to-severe hot flashes, vaginal dryness and discomfort, and preventing bone loss.
assertions.note: The FDA notes approved indications include hot flashes, vaginal symptoms, and bone loss prevention, with no indication for skin changes.

units.text:
A colleague says tirzepatide is 'GRADE A', so its effect on the face must be well established. What is wrong with that reasoning?
Explanation: An evidence grade belongs to a statement, not to a molecule. SURMOUNT-1 supports an A for weight loss; facial change rests on a 20-patient imaging study and a patient survey (C to D), and no randomized trial has measured the face.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Nothing: a drug's grade applies to all of its effects.
Explanation: Grades attach to a specific outcome in a specific population. The pivotal trials measured weight and never the face.
Correct answer: Grades attach to outcomes: weight loss is A from large randomized trials, while facial change rests on small observational studies.
Explanation: Correct. One grade per outcome.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Tirzepatide has no GRADE A evidence for anything.
Explan…

assertions.text: Tirzepatide has Grade A evidence for weight loss/management supported by large randomized controlled trials such as SURMOUNT-1.
assertions.quote: PEARL 8 — GLP-1 agonists earned their grade A. Semaglutide and tirzepatide have randomized weight and cardiometabolic outcome data — the strongest "regenerative-adjacent" pharmacology here.
assertions.note: The guide assigns Grade A to tirzepatide based on randomized weight and cardiometabolic data.

assertions.text: The imaging study examining midfacial volume changes in patients on GLP-1 agonists evaluated 20 patients.
assertions.quote: Twenty patients with available imaging were included in the analysis.
assertions.note: Sharma et al. included 20 patients with available pre- and post-prescription imaging in their analysis.

assertions.text: Evidence characterizing facial changes and skin impacts associated with GLP-1 therapy includes a patient-reported outcome survey.
assertions.quote: Our study was conducted through an IRB-approved, voluntary, anonymous survey developed via collaboration between obesity medicine physicians and dermatologists.
assertions.note: Rao et al. evaluated patient-reported aesthetic and dermatologic changes using a voluntary survey.

assertions.text: No randomized trials or prior objective quantitative studies have measured facial volume changes with GLP-1 therapy.
assertions.quote: No objective data exist to quantitatively characterize midface volume loss in these patients.
assertions.note: Sharma et al. notes that no prior objective quantitative data exist characterizing midfacial volume loss.

units.text:
Which statement about the gut–skin link is best supported by the evidence?
Explanation: High-fat feeding raises circulating endotoxin in mice and briefly in healthy men; a leading review finds it unproven that restoring barrier function improves disease outside the gut, and Cochrane found little or no patient-rated benefit from probiotics in eczema.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Probiotic capsules reliably clear eczema by repairing the gut barrier.
Explanation: Pooled trials show little or no difference in patient-rated eczema symptoms.
Correct answer: Metabolic endotoxaemia is shown in mice and small human studies, but restoring the gut barrier has not been shown to improve disease outside the gut.
Explanation: Correct. Mechanism in mice and short-term human physiology; no proof that barrier repair helps the skin.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): A zonulin b…

assertions.text: High-fat feeding chronically raises circulating endotoxin in mice.
assertions.quote: We found that normal endotoxemia increased or decreased during the fed or fasted state, respectively, on a nutritional basis and that a 4-week high-fat diet chronically increased plasma LPS concentration two to three times, a threshold that we have defined as metabolic endotoxemia.
assertions.note: A 4-week high-fat diet increased plasma LPS concentration two to three times in mice.

assertions.text: A high-fat meal briefly increases circulating endotoxin in healthy men.
assertions.quote: Baseline endotoxin concentrations were 8.2 pg/mL (interquartile range: 3.4-13.5 pg/mL) but increased significantly (P < 0.05) by approximately 50% after a high-fat meal or after a high-fat meal with cigarettes but not after no meal or cigarettes alone.
assertions.note: Plasma endotoxin concentrations increased significantly by about 50% over 4 hours following a high-fat meal in healthy men.

assertions.text: It remains unproven that restoring intestinal barrier function improves clinical manifestations of diseases outside the gut.
assertions.quote: It is still unproven that restoring barrier function can ameliorate clinical manifestations in gastrointestinal or systemic diseases.
assertions.note: The review states it is unproven that restoring barrier function ameliorates clinical manifestations in gastrointestinal or systemic diseases.

assertions.text: A Cochrane review of pooled trials found little or no patient-rated benefit from probiotics for eczema symptoms.
assertions.quote: Probiotics probably make little or no difference in participant- or parent-rated symptoms of eczema (13 trials; 754 participants): symptom severity on a scale from 0 to 20 was 0.44 points lower after probiotic treatment (95% confidence interval (CI) -1.22 to 0.33; moderate-quality evidence).
assertions.note: The Cochrane review found probiotics probably make little or no difference in participant- or parent-rated eczema symptoms.

assertions.text: A widely used commercial zonulin ELISA detects proteins other than zonulin.
assertions.quote: Our study suggests that the zonulin ELISA does not recognize pre-haptoglobin2, rather structural (and possibly functional) analog proteins belonging to the mannose-associated serine protease family, with properdin being the most likely possible candidate.
assertions.note: The study demonstrated that the commercial ELISA did not detect pre-haptoglobin2 (zonulin) and instead detected other proteins such as properdin.

units.text:
Which statement about topical GHK-Cu keeps its evidence and its regulatory status apart correctly?
Explanation: Mechanism, human evidence and regulatory status are separate registers; GHK-Cu scores differently on each.
Correct answer: It is GRADE C on small trials, and in the US its non-injectable form sits in 503A Category 1, which means under evaluation.
Explanation: Correct. Two separate answers: small-trial human evidence, and an enforcement posture that is not an approval.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Its Category 1 listing shows FDA has found it effective for skin.
Explanation: Category 1 means FDA is still evaluating; it says nothing about efficacy.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Its copper-enzyme mechanism makes its evidence grade A.
Explanation: A plausible mechanism is not human evidence; the trials are small (C).

assertions.text: Human clinical trials evaluating topical GHK-Cu are small.
assertions.quote: Thirteen patients completed the study.
assertions.note: Miller et al. report a randomized trial evaluating topical GHK-Cu in only 13 completed patients.

assertions.text: In the United States, non-injectable GHK-Cu is in 503A Category 1 for bulk drug substances under evaluation.
assertions.quote: Example: GHK-copper sits in Category 1 for non-injectable routes, so FDA does not currently intend to act against its use in compounding pending evaluation.
assertions.note: The Peptide Pocket Guide notes that non-injectable GHK-copper sits in Category 1 pending evaluation.

assertions.text: FDA 503A Category 1 designates an enforcement-discretion posture while a substance is under evaluation, rather than an approval of efficacy.
assertions.quote: Categories 1, 2 and 3 are something else: enforcement-discretion postures described in FDA guidance while nominations are evaluated.
assertions.note: The source explains that Category 1 denotes an enforcement-discretion posture during evaluation rather than statutory approval.

units.text:
Oral collagen trials pooled together look positive. What did splitting them by funding and quality show?
Explanation: Funding and study quality can explain a pooled effect; ask who ran the trial before what it showed.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The benefit held in every subgroup.
Explanation: It did not: independent and high-quality trials showed no effect.
Correct answer: The benefit appeared only in pharmaceutical-funded and lower-quality trials.
Explanation: Correct — Myung and Park, 2025, 23 RCTs.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Independent trials showed harm.
Explanation: No harm signal was reported; the finding is about absence of benefit.

assertions.text: In pooled meta-analyses, oral collagen trials show positive effects on skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles.
assertions.quote: In a meta-analysis of all 23 RCTs, collagen supplements significantly improved skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles.
assertions.note: A pooled meta-analysis of all 23 RCTs found significant improvements across hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles.

assertions.text: In the subgroup analysis by Myung and Park (2025), trials not funded by pharmaceutical companies showed no effect on skin parameters, whereas pharmaceutical-funded trials showed significant effects.
assertions.quote: However, in the subgroup meta-analysis by funding source, studies not receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies revealed no effect of collagen supplements for improving skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles, while those receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies did show significant effects.
assertions.note: Subgroup meta-analysis by funding source found no effect in independent trials, whereas pharma-funded trials showed significant effects.

assertions.text: In the meta-analysis by Myung and Park (2025), high-quality trials showed no significant effect in any category, while benefits were observed in lower-quality trials.
assertions.quote: Similarly, high-quality studies revealed no significant effect in all categories, while low-quality studies revealed a significant improvement in elasticity.
assertions.note: High-quality trials showed no significant effect across all categories, whereas low-quality trials showed significant improvement in elasticity.

units.text:
Which statement about afamelanotide and Melanotan II is accurate?
Explanation: Approval attaches to a specific product and indication; a shared receptor transfers neither evidence nor legal standing.
Correct answer: Afamelanotide is approved (EU 2014, US 2019) only for erythropoietic protoporphyria; Melanotan II is approved for no indication, and regulators in the US, UK and Australia have warned about it.
Explanation: Correct. Same receptor family, different molecules, and only one has an approval, for one rare disease.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Afamelanotide's US approval covers cosmetic tanning.
Explanation: The US indication is to increase pain-free light exposure in adults with EPP; tanning is not an approved use.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Melanotan II became approvable once FDA reviewed it for compounding.
Explanation: Its compounding nominat…

assertions.text: Afamelanotide received European Union marketing authorization in 2014 exclusively for erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP).
assertions.quote: The European Commission granted a marketing authorisation valid throughout the European Union for Scenesse on 22 December 2014.
assertions.note: The European Commission granted marketing authorization for Scenesse in December 2014 for EPP.

assertions.text: Afamelanotide's US indication is to increase pain-free light exposure in adult patients with erythropoietic protoporphyria, not cosmetic tanning.
assertions.quote: SCENESSE® is indicated to increase pain free light exposure in adult patients with a history of phototoxic reactions from erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP).
assertions.note: The approved US indication is strictly for light exposure in adults with phototoxic reactions from EPP.

assertions.text: Melanotan II has no approved indications and regulators in the US, UK, and Australia have issued warnings against it.
assertions.quote: These products may cause serious side effects, so our advice to those who have used Melanotan II injections or nasal sprays is to stop using them immediately and if you have suffered side effects, speak to your doctor and report them to the MHRA through our Yellow Card Scheme.
assertions.note: Warnings and unauthorized status are documented for UK and US regulators, but the Australian advisory cannot be verified because the cited source is unavailable.

assertions.text: Melanotan II's compounding nomination was withdrawn, and the FDA lists serious safety risks associated with it.
assertions.quote: Compounded drugs containing Melanotan II may pose risk for immunogenicity for certain routes of administration due to the potential for aggregation or peptide-related impurities. Published case reports discuss serious adverse events including melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, sympathomimetic toxidrome and priapism.
assertions.note: The FDA lists Melanotan II under bulk drug substances nominated but withdrawn, detailing significant safety risks.

units.text:
A patient asks about a PTD-DBM hair spray. Which grade fits its evidence, and why?
Explanation: Grade the human evidence, then say who produced it; a strong mechanism with no trial in people is D.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): A, because it acts on the central Wnt pathway of hair growth.
Explanation: A plausible pathway is mechanism, and grades rest on human evidence.
Correct answer: D: one 2017 study in mice and scalp tissue from the developer's group, and no human trial published or registered as of September 2026.
Explanation: Correct. Animal and tissue data only, from one group with a commercial link.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): C, because small human trials show regrowth.
Explanation: No human trial of PTD-DBM exists, small or large.

assertions.text: PTD-DBM evidence is graded D because it has preclinical data only, with no clinical trials in humans.
assertions.quote: Clinical caveat. Mechanistically the most interesting investigational hair-loss compound on this list, but human efficacy data is thin — most use is via compounding pharmacies. Effective only combined with a Wnt-pathway modulator (typically valproic acid). Trial stage: preclinical only; no human RCTs.
assertions.note: The clinical reference guide grades PTD-DBM as Grade D, noting only preclinical data and no human RCTs.

assertions.text: Preclinical evidence for PTD-DBM comes from a 2017 study evaluating it in mice and human scalp cells.
assertions.quote: The inhibitory effects of CXXC5 on alkaline phosphatase activity and cell proliferation were demonstrated using human hair follicle dermal papilla cells. Moreover, CXXC5 -/- mice displayed accelerated hair regrowth, and treatment with valproic acid, a glycogen synthase kinase 3β inhibitor that activates the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, further induced hair regrowth in the CXXC5 -/- mice.
assertions.note: The 2017 study demonstrated CXXC5 inhibition in human dermal papilla cells and mice.

assertions.text: No human trial of PTD-DBM has been published or registered as of September 2026.
assertions.quote: Trial stage: preclinical only; no human RCTs.
assertions.note: The guide confirms that only preclinical data exists with no human trials, but its verification cutoff is August 2026 rather than September 2026.

assertions.text: The developer's group that produced the PTD-DBM animal and tissue data has a commercial link.
assertions.note: None of the provided sources mention a commercial link or financial interest associated with the developer's group.

recheck.note: The provided sources do not mention whether the research group behind PTD-DBM has a commercial link.

units.text:
In the US, as of September 2026, which statement about growth-hormone secretagogues and 503A compounding is accurate?
Explanation: Popularity and compounding volume are not regulatory standing; check the live FDA lists and name the date.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Ipamorelin and CJC-1295 are on the 503A bulks list, because clinics compound them widely.
Explanation: Neither is on the list. FDA's advisory committee voted against ipamorelin in 2024, and both 503A nominations were withdrawn.
Correct answer: None of them is on the 503A bulks list; ibutamoren is in FDA's Category 2 for a heart-failure signal, and the ipamorelin and CJC-1295 nominations were withdrawn.
Explanation: Correct, dated to FDA's category documents of April and May 2026.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Sermorelin is an FDA-approved product marketed for adult anti-ageing.
Explanation: No…

assertions.text: FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee voted against placing ipamorelin on the 503A bulks list in 2024.
assertions.quote: The majority of the Committee members voted against placing Ipamorelin (free base) on the 503A Bulks List.
assertions.note: FDA advisory committee minutes confirm the committee voted against placing ipamorelin on the 503A bulks list in October 2024.

assertions.text: The 503A nominations for ipamorelin and CJC-1295 were withdrawn by their nominators.
assertions.quote: This list of bulk drug substances previously in category 2 of the interim policies were withdrawn by the nominators.
assertions.note: FDA lists both substances in the table of bulk drug substances that were nominated but withdrawn by nominators.

assertions.text: Ibutamoren is placed in FDA 503A Category 2 due to a safety signal for congestive heart failure.
assertions.quote: Ibutamoren mesylate poses significant safety risks due to the potential for congestive heart failure in certain patients. The agency is aware of a randomized, placebo-controlled trial assessing ibutamoren mesylate for the treatment of patients recovering from hip fracture that “was terminated early due to a potential safety signal of congestive heart failure.”
assertions.note: FDA documents place ibutamoren in Category 2 due to a potential safety signal for congestive heart failure in clinical trial data.

assertions.text: Former FDA approvals for sermorelin were indicated for growth hormone deficiency in children and for diagnostic testing of pituitary somatotroph function.

units.text:
In GRADE, what does a certainty rating attach to?
Explanation: Name the outcome before you name the grade; risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias can each lower it.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): A single well-run trial.
Explanation: GRADE rates a body of evidence, never one study on its own.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The molecule, across all its uses.
Explanation: The same molecule can be high certainty for one outcome and very low for another.
Correct answer: A body of evidence for a specific outcome.
Explanation: Correct. Certainty belongs to an outcome, across the studies that address it.

No adequately sized trial with clinical skin-ageing outcomes was found (September 2026). In mice, clearing senescent cells during healing slowed wound closure. units.text: Most 'cortisol face' is puffiness from sleep, alcohol, salt and weight, as the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide describes it. Endogenous Cushing's syndrome is rare (two to three new cases per million people a year), and its commonest form comes from a glucocorticoid the patient is using, so ask about tablets, inhalers, injections and creams, including skin-lighteners. The features that best discriminate Cushing's are easy bruising, facial plethora, proximal muscle weakness and reddish-purple striae wider than 1 cm; a round face alone is a weak signal. If several are present and progressing, the next step is formal testing arranged by a prescriber and an endocrinologist, not a supplement or a consumer cortisol panel. Local skin cortisol (11β-HSD1) is a research mechanism with no approved treatment.

units.text: Signs of growth-hormone excess include puffy, thickened skin of the face, hands and feet, oily skin, more sweating, skin tags, acanthosis nigricans, tight rings or shoes, night-time tingling and carpal tunnel symptoms. On GH-axis drugs, fluid retention with swelling and joint pain is common and usually settles when treatment stops. The Endocrine Society recommends IGF-1 testing when typical acral and facial features are present, so route these patients to a prescriber or to endocrinology. On cancer, keep four answers apart: the IGF-1 receptor drives cell growth (mechanism); higher natural IGF-1 goes with modestly higher risk of some cancers (observation); GH replacement in true deficiency has not shown a clear risk in large cohorts; and for secretagogues or IGF-1 LR3 used for skin, long-term cancer data do not exist (open question).

assertions.quote: Insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-I and its main binding protein, IGFBP-3, modulate cell growth and survival, and are thought to be important in tumour development.
assertions.note: The meta-analysis states that IGF-1 and its binding protein modulate cell growth and survival.

units.text: GRADE rates certainty for a specific outcome across a body of evidence: high, moderate, low or very low (the Hormonaly guides print A to D). Randomized trials start high; certainty drops for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or suspected publication bias. Industry-sponsored studies more often report favourable results (Cochrane, 2017), so ask who ran and paid for the trials. A grade is separate from legal status: check both, and never let a mechanism raise a grade. This course gives no doses or sourcing advice.

assertions.text: GRADE evaluates certainty across a body of evidence into four categories: high, moderate, low, and very low.
assertions.quote: GRADE specifies four categories-high, moderate, low, and very low-that are applied to a body of evidence, not to individual studies.
assertions.note: GRADE defines four quality categories applied to a body of evidence rather than individual studies.

assertions.text: The Hormonaly guides print GRADE ratings using the letters A through D.
assertions.quote: Every entry is rated A-D by GRADE methodology, which reflects the strength of clinical evidence -- not molecular plausibility, popularity, compounding availability, or fashion.
assertions.note: The guide explains that every entry is rated from A to D using GRADE methodology.

assertions.text: Under GRADE, randomized trials begin as high certainty, and certainty drops for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, or publication bias.
assertions.quote: Randomized trials begin as high-quality evidence, observational studies as low quality. "Quality" as used in GRADE means more than risk of bias and so may also be compromised by imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness of study results, and publication bias.
assertions.note: The GRADE guidelines describe randomized trials as starting high and listing these specific factors that compromise quality.

assertions.text: According to a 2017 Cochrane review, industry-sponsored studies more often report favorable results.
assertions.quote: Sponsorship of drug and device studies by the manufacturing company leads to more favorable efficacy results and conclusions than sponsorship by other sources.
assertions.note: The Cochrane review concluded that industry sponsorship leads to more favorable efficacy results and conclusions.

assertions.text: An evidence grade is separate from legal status, and a mechanism alone never raises a grade.
assertions.quote: An FDA-approved drug may carry a lower grade for a particular off-label use than an investigational compound supported by stronger human evidence; regulatory status and evidentiary certainty are separate axes. Mechanistic appeal alone never raises a grade.
assertions.note: The guide explicitly notes regulatory status and evidentiary certainty are separate axes and mechanistic appeal never raises a grade.

units.text: In the US, a 503A pharmacy may compound only from a substance that meets a USP or NF monograph, or else is a component of an approved drug, or else is on the 503A bulks list (six substances, none a peptide, as of September 2026), and it needs a valid certificate of analysis. A certificate is the supplier's report on one lot: mass spectrometry for identity, HPLC for purity, plus endotoxin and microbial results. It cannot prove your vial is that lot, how it was stored, or that it is sterile or lawful. 'Research use only' products are labelled not for use in humans, and 'off-label' applies only to approved drugs. In the UK, an unlicensed medicine reaches a patient as a 'special', made by a licensed specials manufacturer to a prescriber's order for one patient's special clinical need, or as a medicine a pharmacist prepares against a prescription; MHRA guidance ranks a UK-licensed medicine, e…

assertions.text: In the US, a 503A compounding pharmacy may compound bulk drug substances only if they meet an applicable USP or NF monograph, are components of an FDA-approved drug, or appear on the 503A bulks list.
assertions.quote:
Under section 503A of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, a bulk drug
substance may be used in compounding only if it meets a USP or NF
monograph, is a component of an FDA-approved drug, or appears on FDA's
503A Bulks List.
assertions.note: Section 503A restricts bulk compounding to substances meeting a monograph, components of approved drugs, or entries on the bulks list.

assertions.text: As of September 2026, the 503A bulks list contains six substances, none of which is a peptide.
assertions.quote:
The 503A bulks list is codified at 21 C.F.R. 216.23 and holds six substances —
Brilliant Blue G, cantharidin, diphenylcyclopropenone,
N-acetyl-D-glucosamine, squaric acid dibutyl ester, thymol iodide — four
topical-only. No peptide is on it.
assertions.note: The 503A bulks list codified at 21 CFR 216.23 lists six substances, none of which is a peptide.

assertions.text: A certificate of analysis is the supplier's report on one lot, detailing mass spectrometry for identity, HPLC for purity, and endotoxin and microbial results.
assertions.quote:
A serious COA tells you what the supplier found on a named lot:
whether the mass matches the expected molecule, how pure the material
was by HPLC, what counter-ion it carries, and what the endotoxin and
microbial results were.
assertions.note: The source defines a serious COA as reporting mass spectrometry for identity, HPLC for purity, and microbial/endotoxin results for a named lot.

assertions.text: A certificate of analysis cannot prove that the vial in hand is that lot, how it was stored, or that it is sterile or lawful.
assertions.quote:
What it cannot establish on its own is that a product
is safe to inject — that turns on sterility, the dose and route, the conditions
the material was held in since testing, and whether the lot tested is the lot in
hand.
assertions.note: The source notes a COA cannot verify sterility, post-testing storage conditions, or whether the lot tested is in hand, but does not state it cannot prove whether it is lawful.

assertions.text: 'Research use only' products are labelled not for use in humans.
assertions.quote: CAUTION: Contains a new drug for investigational use only in laboratory research animals, or for tests in vitro. Not for use in humans.
assertions.note: FDA regulations require drugs for investigational research use in animals or in vitro tests to be labeled not for use in humans.

assertions.text: The term 'off-label' applies only to unapproved uses of approved drugs.
assertions.quote: Unapproved use of an approved drug is often called “off-label” use.
assertions.note: The FDA defines off-label use specifically as the unapproved use of an approved drug.

assertions.text: In the UK, an unlicensed medicine reaches a patient as a 'special', made by a licensed specials manufacturer to a prescriber's order for one patient's special clinical need.
assertions.quote: 1.3  This Guidance Note provides advice on the manufacture, importation, distribution and supply of unlicensed medicinal products for human use (commonly described as “specials”) which have been specially manufactured or imported to the order of a doctor, dentist, nurse independent prescriber, pharmacist independent prescriber or supplementary prescriber for the treatment of individual patients.
assertions.note: MHRA guidance defines specials as unlicensed medicines made to a prescriber's order for individual patient treatment.

assertions.text: In the UK, an unlicensed medicine can also reach a patient as a medicine prepared by a pharmacist against a prescription.
assertions.quote: 4.5  A holder of a Manufacturer’s “Specials” Licence may also be a registered pharmacy supplying unlicensed medicinal products prepared under the exemption provided by section 10 of the 1968 Medicines Act and regulation 4 of the Human Medicines Regulations 2012.
assertions.note: Registered pharmacies may supply unlicensed medicines prepared under the Section 10 exemption of the Medicines Act 1968.

assertions.text: MHRA guidance ranks a UK-licensed medicine, even used off-label, ahead of an unlicensed medicine.
assertions.quote: 2.4  Although MHRA does not recommend “off-label” (outside the licensed indications) use of products, if a UK licensed product can meet the clinical need, even off-label, it should be used instead of an unlicensed product (see Appendix 2).
assertions.note: MHRA guidance states a UK-licensed product, even used off-label, should be preferred over an unlicensed product.

assertions.text: In the UK, specials may not be advertised.
assertions.quote: (3) Condition B is that no advertisement relating to the medicinal product is published by any person.
assertions.note: Condition B of Regulation 167 prohibits the publication of any advertisement relating to a special medicinal product.
